utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, have the accused brought in. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to say good morning to the interpreters and be sure that everybody can hear me. Do the booths hear me? The Judges have exceptionally agreed to have a photographer from the agency here, conditional on the approval of the accused who did agree to the photographers being here. Now we can resume our work and continue with the questions being asked of the General. Perhaps he should come in first. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We're going to continue. Mr. Nobilo, continue, please. You still have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, yesterday, we saw several combat reports. In the hours to follow, we will see more of such reports relating to the April war. I would like you to tell the Tribunal, with a five-year perspective, were all these reports reliable, or were there sometimes some pieces of information in them that were not so correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the contents of the reports which we're addressing today was not always very accurate, and the reasons for it are as follows: When I talked about the organisation, I pointed out the deficiency of fully trained personnel, and this reflected on the reports. Let's say a report that came from a subordinate commander into the command depended on the training of these officers. There will be examples where we will have reports written by a better trained officer. We will have such reports, but, for instance, the report from the Travnik Brigade written by Zvonimir Macic, if I'm not mistaken, this is the kind of language that he uses. He was a journalist. This posed a problem for us at the time, but those are the only reports which we had available at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You talked about this organisation. The fact that there were some relations or friendly relations, did that have any effect?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, the organisation of the HVO was based on the territorial principle in villages, so friends and relations were part of these units. These reports reflected that. In other words, they were not always fully accurate. They did not always reflect the actual situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yesterday, we saw the reports of the Viteska Brigade from different points in the field, and I would now like to show you one that came from the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would the usher please help me distribute this document which was compiled on the 16th of April? It refers to the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D280, D280A for the French version, and D280B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'll read it. It is short.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Before counsel starts, the English booth has not received its copy. Hold on just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is addressed to Central Bosnia Operative Zone. It is dated the 16th of April, 1993, and the body of text runs as follows: "Acting in accordance with your order number 01-04-243/93 of 16 April, 1993," even though "1993" is not clear, something is crossed out and then "1993" has been entered, "we hereby report the Muslim armed forces attempted to launch an attack on the military police units located in the Bungalow in the early morning hours. The attack met with response, and combat procedures and actions were undertaken to expel the same. The Muslim armed forces, MOS, barricaded themselves in a mosque in Ahmici and in a primary school, from where they have been firing from small arms weapons and snipers. They have been opening light fire from the direction of the villages of Vrhovine and Pirici, and snipers have been constantly firing from the woods and clearings above the village. So far, three policemen have been killed and three wounded, one of whom seriously. The personnel is in the field," and then "Commander," and a signature and a stamp. First off, Brigadier, did you receive this document on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. We received this document on 16 April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this the signature of the commander or somebody else's?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This is not the signature of the commander of this unit. I believe that it may have been signed by the duty officer of the unit. It is of the 4th Battalion of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does this copy fully correspond to the original which you received from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I said that I recalled this report, and on that basis, I say that this is an exact copy of the original which we had received on 16 April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me take you to the preamble of this report. It refers to a previous order number. What is that in reference to?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I talked about the conflicts which erupted in the Vitez and Busovaca municipalities --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is not necessary to go into that, because we saw that slide yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: We saw that there was a conflict on the road near Ahmici. The commander of the Operative Zone received this information, but he was interested in the follow-up. He wanted to know what would happen later. As we were receiving reports from the military police only occasionally, the commander of the Operative Zone, in order to receive full information about what was going on on the Vitez-Busovaca road, issued an order which was numbered 01-04-243/93, in which he ordered the commander of the military police unit to fully report on the developments. The report itself is in response to this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: While we're waiting on this document, Brigadier, could you please tell the Court, apart from this report, did any other report arrive at the command of the Operative Zone from the military police battalion in Ahmici on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D281, D281A for the French version, and D281B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, so far we have been going through reports of the 16th. This is an order dated the 16th of April, 1993; time, 1945 hours. It is a combat order for the defence of Kuber, and it was to be delivered to the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade in Busovaca. The text reads: "1) The extremist Muslim forces are advancing from the direction of Gornja Zenica toward Kuber with the objective of completely capturing it and cutting it off. 2) Your task is as follows: To reinforce the defence of Kuber with your best prepared and most able forces and to persist in its defence. The minimum strength of the forces is to be one company, 120 soldiers. 3) You are to coordinate your actions with the Viteska Brigade and ensure that Kuber does not fall. 4) After holding the defence lines, you are to report to me in writing," and it is signed by Colonel Blaskic, and there is a stamp affixed to it. First, does this copy fully reflect the original combat order of the 16th of April at 1945 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. This is a copy which fully reflects the original document which was drafted on the 16th of April, 1993 at 1945 hours. I recognise the signature of General Blaskic. I recognise the stamp of the Operative Zone. The handwriting in the top corner is my handwriting on the orders of the commander of the Operative Zone, because we had problems with communications with certain units. This is a verbal warning for implementing and submitting reports on the combat order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the goal of this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: What we wanted to ensure is, besides the written order, we wanted to verbally warn them and to emphasise, because we wanted to know what was really going on on the ground so that we could counter with the proper action. On verbal orders of the commander, I wrote this down in handwriting, and this is reflected in the copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, why are we dealing so much with Kuber here? What was so important about Kuber, and which units were supposed to go there to this hill or mountain?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mount Kuber is a key feature in the Lasva River Valley for both the defensive communication lines in the settlements in the valley. Yesterday, Your Honours, I spoke about the main directions of attack of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and one of them was from Zenica directly across Mount Kuber. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, it would be very good if you could, again, point on the scale model, if you could show us Mount Kuber, Gornja Zenica, and where these troops could have gone if they captured Mount Kuber?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this is Mount Kuber (indicating). It is situated exactly between Zenica, a large city, and the Lasva Valley. Its foothills are right next to the Vitez-Busovaca-Zenica road. If you have your forces positioned on this mountain, you have full control over this road and, thereby, you're always in a position, with smaller forces, to cut communications along this road and interrupt traffic. That is why this mountain has such importance, and that is why the commander of the Operative Zone decided to insist, in particular, on the defence of this mountain. As you probably noticed in the text, it says, "Kuber must not fall." In military terminology, if you give such an order that something must not fall, it means that forces must not withdraw from there, even at the cost of life. If a soldier is given such an order, he knows what he has to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you please explain to the Court, Mount Kuber is exposed to which forces, the attack of which forces, and where would those forces have to come from to attack Mount Kuber? If you do hold Mount Kuber, which are the spots where it is easy to intersect the main communication line?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The main forces we expected to come from Zenica, Zenica (indicating), and their task was to follow this direction, Zenica-Kuber-Vitez, to move along those lines and attack these locations. That was their task, to cross over Mount Kuber and to link up with local forces in the Muslim Bosniak villages in Vitez municipality. The best chance for intersecting the Vitez-Busovaca road is around Kaonik and in the vicinity of the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could the usher please assist the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, tell us, please, why did Blaskic give this order as late as 1945 hours for the defence of the Lasva region?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, if you recall my presentation yesterday, I was speaking about the group of officers from the Operative Zone command and representatives of the BH army, they held a meeting at the UNPROFOR base where they agreed on a complete cease-fire. On the basis of that report, the commander of the Operative Zone issued an order to halt fire and hostilities. However, reports from the field indicated that the BH army, far from suspending action and respecting the agreed cease-fire, was actually mobilising strong forces from Zenica with a view to fulfilling its plan, and that is, to gain full control of the territory of the municipalities of Busovaca and Vitez. Therefore, the engaged forces are expanding their initial goal. From the roots they were following, it was evident that the territory of Busovaca municipality was at stake. In such a situation, the commander of the Operative Zone had no other choice but to issue such a strong-worded order to defend that mountain with all available forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, you're a military man, so let me ask you a military theoretical question: If an attack had been planned on the Muslim forces in the Lasva Valley, would the commander have, in advance, positioned 120 soldiers on Mount Kuber as security?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Certainly that is the only reasonable logic to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D282, D282A for the French version, D282B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We are reading parts of the document numbered 282. The command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia or, rather, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, on the 16th of April, 1993, at 1940 hours, writes to the commander of the 4th Military Police Battalion and the commander of the Travnicka Brigade for Information. The heading is "Withdrawal of Troops of the Travnik Military Police Company to Vitez." The text: "Due to the intensified combat by Muslim forces in the region of Vitez municipality and the need to provide reinforcement to the troops of the Viteska Brigade, I hereby order: 1) The unit from the 4th Military Police Battalion, currently stationed in the city of Travnik, shall be immediately transferred to Vitez. All activities related to this transfer shall be carried out in utmost secrecy." We won't read the rest, because I do not consider it to be relevant. What does this mean, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This order was drafted in the Operative Zone command of Central Bosnia on the 16th of April, 1993 at 19:40 hours. I personally drafted this order and it was signed by General Blaskic. It was addressed to the commander of the 4th Military Police Battalion. Due to the intensified combat operations and movements of strong forces from Zenica towards Vitez and because the units of the Viteska Brigade were not ready, in order to assist them the commander of the Operative Zone issued the order that units of the military police that had been in Travnik should be transferred to Vitez to assist the Viteska Brigade in defending the town of Vitez. One can also infer from this order that the commander of the Operative Zone had planned an attack of the BH army on Vitez. These forces would have been transferred earlier rather than on the 16th of April at 19.40 when the situation was already extremely complicated, unfavourable and uncertain with regard to the towns of Vitez and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: There appears to be an error in the transcript as Colleague Hayman tells me. It says that the commander had planned the attack, but you said if the commander had planned the attack. So could the transcript be corrected because it is a key word. Let me ask you the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you conclude from this order in connection with the planning?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: If the commander of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia had planned a conflict with the BH army, if he had planned to attack the BH army in Vitez, he would have transferred these forces earlier on. As he didn't do that and as he hadn't planned an attack on the army of Bosnia-Hercegovina in the area of Busovaca in Vitez, he found himself in the situation that on 16th of April, after the attack of the BH army in the territory of Vitez and Busovaca and because of the movement of strong forces, he issued such an order to defend Vitez and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you are seeking assistance from other units from another area, does that mean that you are weak where you are?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely why assistance was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 283, 283A for the French version, 283B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we have an order by Colonel Blaskic of the 16th of April, '93, on 2015 hours addressed to the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade in Novi Travnik. The subject heading is, "Order for Increased Control of Territory." The preamble reads: "Proceeding from intelligence information on possible routes for the transfer of Muslim forces to the territory of Vitez municipality, Gornja Veceriska and Veceriska and with the objective of detecting in a timely fashion and preventing the said forces from crossing, I hereby order." The order has to do with the deployment of units of the Novi Travnik Brigade and ends with item 4, which says, "Send me a report on the execution of this order by 2400 hours on 16th April, 1993." Please tell me, first, whether this copy is a faithful copy of the original document written by Colonel Blaskic on the 16th of April at 2015 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The copy is faithful to the original. I drafted it and it was signed by General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, where were those forces being transferred from? Could you perhaps indicate on the relief Gornja Vecerska and Donji Vecriska and how those forces were expected to be infiltrated into the territory?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Let me just say that the infiltration of those forces would come from an auxiliary route. Mr. President, Your Honours, Novi Travnik, the town of Novi Travnik is here and the area of the Novi Travnik municipality is here. According to this order and on the basis of intelligence reports, the commander of the Operative Zone expected BH army units to come from Novi Travnik and to transfer a part of their forces along this route, Buckka Ravan towards Gornja and Donji Vecerska, whereby it would link up with the forces in the area of Donji Vecerska and in the area of Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the BH army already have its forces in Donji Vecerska and Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, the BH army already had local forces in Donji Vecerska and in Kruscica in addition to -- additional to local forces, it also had the forces that had arrived there on the 14th or the 15th that we mentioned previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Donji Vecerska as a locality, why was it particularly important in Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Donji Vecerska, which is here, was important for two reasons: One, is that that village was right next to the fence of the explosives factory. This is the explosive factory and it was right next to the compound. And because at a distance of 1.5 kilometres, close to those forces were significant forces of the BH army at Grbavica, which already had control of this road passing through Grbavica. And this is the main road linking Vitez and Novi Travnik with Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Brigadier, tell us, did the BH army have the greater chances of manoeuvring from Novi Travnik as it didn't have a front against the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, the BH army had a whole brigade in Novi Travnik, which was not engaged on the front-line of defence against the army of Republika Srpska in the area of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And who held the frontlines in the area of Novi Travnik towards the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The defence lines against the army of Republika Srpska from March, 1992, that means for almost a year, were held by HVO units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, do you know which municipality those HVO units were from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't quite get your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know which municipalities the HVO units came from that were holding the fronts against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The HVO units were local units from Novi Travnik. I am referring to HVO units, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D284, 284A for the French version and 284B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The document was drafted in the night between the 16th and the 17th of April of 1993. The time indicated is 0400 hours. It was written by Colonel Blaskic, addressed to the Busovaca and Viteska Brigade; therefore, in two municipalities and it reads: The heading, "defence of consolidated positions order: Based on our information in the course of the day the enemy will make intense military preparations for an offensive." That is the first sentence. In the third paragraph it says: "The survival and the life of Croatian inhabitants of the Lasva Valley is at stake and it is being resolved today, maybe for the last time." We are leaving out two paragraphs and then we come to the next one, which says: To the Busovaca Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade the focus of the defence is on Kuber, which is to be defended by unarmed soldiers if necessary as reinforcements. Other access roads are to be blocked and full control is to be taken of Gornja Rovna and Pezici. To the commander of the Viteska Brigade: "Use main forces to defend access roads to and from the town, especially from the direction of Poculica and Pirici and towards Vranjska. To this end, link up with military police forces and with auxiliary forces keep under blockade the forces in the areas of Viteska. If possible, seize Donja Veceriska. The fire brigade centre, Kruscica and Vranjska." And underlined, "the blockade being a priority." And, finally, the last sentence of this order: "We have accomplished 80 percent of our task and we need to exert special efforts today. Special caution should be addressed to soldiers about the treatment of civilians (the elderly women and children who are not to be killed because that is a crime)." The word "crime" is in blocked capitals. Signed "Commander Colonel Tihomir Blaskic". Brigadier, have you seen this document before and is this photocopy a true replica of the original document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I have seen the document. I saw it on the 17th of April when I woke up in the morning. This copy is a faithful copy of the original document drafted in the Operative Zone command. It was signed by General Blaskic. He personally drafted it. The stamp is of the Operative Zone command. Obviously he didn't have anyone to type it. It was hand-written, typed on Packet, given to him to sign and then it was dispatched to the indicated addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you said "he typed it on Packet," you mean the computer software that you called Packet Radio?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that can be seen from the letters which are obviously printed with a computer printer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How were most of your documents written? What devices did you have?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Our command was in very short supply with office equipment. And as can be seen, we had a small mechanical typewriter and we had a larger mechanical typewriter. That's all we had at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please concentrate on the third paragraph from the bottom with instructions to the Viteska Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Obviously the commander of the Viteska Brigade had the task of defending the approaches to the town with his main forces and especially from the directions of Poculica and Preocica and toward Vranjska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you perhaps get up and show Their Honours which is the main direction that the commander is expecting forces to come from on the 17th and why he is issuing these orders to the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Poculica and Preocica and towards Vranjska. This is Poculica. This is Poculica an inhabited locality on the main road, linking Vitez, via Vjetrenica to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, whose forces were in Poculica on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Local forces of the BH army which were to link up with the main forces coming from Zenica and then to continue on from Poculica via Preocica -- this is Preocica, which is another village where the BH army had its forces. So this was the route, Poculica, Poculica towards Vranjska and they would intersect the road at the railway station in the Town of Vitez and thereby they would gain control of a part of the Town of Vitez and link up with forces in Vranjska. So this is the route, the shortest route.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell the Court in Vranjska, were there any BH army forces there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: There were both local forces and forces brought in as reinforcements on the 13th or the 14th that we have already discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please go back to your seat. Thank you. Will you please look at the last sentence. Blaskic is cautioning, especially about the treatment of civilians, and says they must not be killed because that is a crime. Why does Blaskic say this after the first day of battle at dawn at 0400 hours in the night of the 17th? Why is he cautioning fighters that it is a crime to kill civilians? Why does Blaskic put this in a combat order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: We know that on the 16th a meeting was held in the UNPROFOR base and that the meeting was attended also by members of the Operative Zone command. On the road from Vitez to the UNPROFOR base in Bila, members of the Operative Zone command, together with UNPROFOR officers, noticed or rather saw two or three bodies, corpses of civilians. I assume that members of the Operative Zone command informed the commander of the Operative Zone of this. And I believe that that was the reason which prompted the commander of the Operative Zone as early as 0400 hours of the 17th to add in addition to combat orders this reference to this problem. Another reason, in my view, why this was done by General Blaskic is that General Blaskic was aware that units of both the BH army and the HVO organised in villages intermingled with the civilian population and that such a danger was a serious possibility. And another reason why I insisted on this was General Blaskic's personal character and integrity and honour as an officer of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 285, 285A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So after this warning overnight, we are going to attempt a reconstruction of the events of the 17th of April. At 600 hours a report arrives in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command and the subject is a regular combat report. It arrived on 17th April at 600 hours. The body of the text reads as follows: "The night was quiet on the territory Novi Travnik Municipality. We received no notification of potential conflicts with the BH army. There were no combat activities by Chetniks on the defence line in the zone of our responsibility" and it is signed by the operations duty officer, Ivica Fabris. Brigadier, does this copy fully reflect the original which you had received at a command of the Operation Zone?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. From the stamp you can see that it was received by us. It was properly registered. It was signed by Ivica Fabris, whom I personally know and I recognise his signature. And I fully recall the contents of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, there was fighting in Vitez and Busovaca in Kuber there is no withdrawal, now how about Novi Travnik? How do you explain this report?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, from this report we can glean that the commander of the Operative Zone had not planned a war with the BH army. Had he planned the war with the BH army, in the time period which we're dealing with, he would have ordered certain combat actions in Novi Travnik as well and there would have been conflict in Novi Travnik as well. There was no conflict in Novi Travnik because the BH army did not attack at Novi Travnik and so the HVO had no task there. And you can see that the command, the commander of this Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade is dealing with a situation of the defence line against the Serbian forces. And when we put that in the context of the entire situation, you see the complexity with which the commander of the Operative Zone needed to deal with. I am going to just point out several key elements of the situation on that day. They are as follows: One, we have large BH army forces in the area of Vitez and Busovaca. We have very large scale conflict. The Viteska Brigade is not fully organised. You may recall that Cerkez received the order to organise the Viteska Brigade only shortly before this. We saw the panic. We saw the disorganisation. Then let me also remind you of the map in 1992, April and March. The main forces, the main weapons are placed towards, deployed towards the Republika Srpska, of Zepce, Usora and all the other defence lines held by the HVO towards the army of Republika Srpska. I recall very well the situation. It was a problem that we had no solution for and we were really in a very difficult situation, especially given that on the 16th of April we were attacked and we were completely surprised by the attack of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D286, D286A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, on 17 April at 600 hours, you received another report, this time from Zepce, from the 111th XP Brigade. Ivo Livancic, in item 3, says, "The relations with the BH army are on a satisfactory level." In item 2, it says, "Our forces are firmly holding the lines of defence. Shifts were changed properly." This is all towards the army of Republika Srpska. Brigadier, did you receive this document from Zepce?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that from the stamp of receipt. We were expecting these reports with great expectations so that we would know what the situation was in a wider area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How do you understand this item 3, that the relations with the BH army were on a satisfactory level?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The BH army had not attacked the 111th Brigade, so the situation was quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: New document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D287, D287A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In contrast to these two reports on a quiet front, you received another report on 17 April at 600 hours. Let me read it for you. It's a combat report, and I will start with the third paragraph: "Several times during the night, we received information about the regrouping of Muslim forces, whereby we could conclude that they will make an attempt at a breakthrough from the direction of Vrhovine and in the Santici-Ahmici direction in order to cut off the Vitez-Kaonik communication and join with Rovna. If they realise their intentions, any traffic communication between Vitez and Busovaca will become impossible. We are doing our best to thwart their efforts. In the area of Grbavica, sizeable forces are concentrated and, according to incoming information, they received troop reinforcements from Bukve, among whom are some Mujahedeen. The Muslim population was evacuated from Grbavica and Divjak. There are indications that Muslim forces may try to cut off the road to Donja Veceriska. With this operation, they hope to establish a corridor, Donja Veceriska-Divjak-Grbavica-Bukve. Our unit in Lovac is under enemy siege and we have no communication with them and no option of logistics support. We are trying to come up with appropriate solutions. Fatigue can be observed among the soldiers but the morale is good. Our wounded have been given medical care." It was signed by Zvonimir Cilic, duty officer. First of all, Brigadier, is this a faithful copy of the original you received on the 17th at 600 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I confirm that on the basis of my remembering this document, which we received at the Operative Zone command. I also personally know Zvonimir Cilic, and I recognise his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, let's go back to the scale model so that we can get a better idea of where these locations are that we're talking about. Brigadier, would you please point what the direction of attack was from Vrhovine to Santici and Ahmici in order to cut off the communication line Vitez-Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This is the village of Vrhovine (indicating). This is the village of Santici (indicating), and this is the village of Ahmici (indicating). Both Ahmici and Santici are on the road, that is, along the road that leads from Vitez to Kaonik and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court what forces were in Vrhovine at that time and throughout the Muslim-Croat war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Vrhovine had the local forces and were reinforced by forces which arrived from Zenica, and their task was to direct their assault operations towards Santici and Ahmici, to cut off the communication line, and to link up to their other forces at Rovna. I would also like to point out to the Trial Chamber that this area of Ahmici and Santici, if you look at it in relation to Rovna, it is no more than 1.5 kilometres wide as the crow flies. The enemy forces, if you are not fully alert and prepared, could take it very easily. I'm pointing out that it is a very narrow area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Apart from this focus of conflict, could you also point out the other flash point, Grbavica and Divjak? The reinforcements from the village of Bukve, could you point out those and the directions from which the Vitez municipality could be threatened?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The village of Grbavica is along the road leading from Vitez to Novi Travnik. The village of Bukve is located about two kilometres from the village of Grbavica due north-east, and you can see what the BH army opted for. Realising the importance of the road that passes through the village of Grbavica, they had already brought their reinforcements there, the forces which they had in Bukve, and these local forces were reinforced by the unit called the Mujahed. Continuing on from Grbavica, they would go to Donja Veceriska and Divjak. Again, let me point out that the distance here is 1.5 to 1.8 kilometres. They are all very narrow strips of land, and if the opponent is not extremely alert and cautious, this task becomes very possible. If you look at Grbavica, Divjak, and Donja Veceriska, if you took all these positions, this explosives factory in Vitez could also be seized, which was one of the strategic goals of the BH army during the war in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you point out the corridor of Bukve, Donja Veceriska, Divjak, does that mean that the key communication line leading from Vitez to Travnik and Novi Travnik would be cut off?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It was already cut, and that was the reason why we had to take steps to find an alternate road along the terrain where there was no road previously, so that we could keep the communication open between Vitez and Novi Travnik. These forces were tasked to reinforce the forces which had already cut off that communication line, and that made the whole situation much more complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At the end, the bottom of the report, it says, "Our units in Lovac are under enemy siege, and we have no communications with them and no options for logistics support." Where were they besieged? Where was it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The facility of Lovac was in Kruscica, and this was a mixed Croat-Muslim village. This was a unit which was a volunteer unit composed of hunters, local villagers. Given the surprising nature of the attack, this unit had remained in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What forces were controlling Kruscica at that time and throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Eighty per cent of the settlement of the village of Kruscica was controlled by the BH army. Your Honours, the village of Kruscica is one of the larger communities in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does the information mean, that 15 men which were there had no chance against a much superior force? What was their situation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The people who remained, these 15 to 20 men, this group, again, points to the fact that the HVO was surprised by the BH army attack, that had we planned an attack, we would have pulled out those men from that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, it is now twenty after eleven. We are going to take a 20-minute break and we'll resume at 11.40. The hearing is suspended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before we resume, Mr. Nobilo, where are we now in respect of the time that you're going to spend with this witness? I know he is very important for you. How is our work going to go forward? You know tomorrow morning is an initial appearance, how do you see things? Because I think that the Prosecutor will have cross-examination to conduct and the judges will have some questions to ask. Perhaps it will be the entire week that we're going to devote to this witness. Please tell us where we are Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are at 17 April 1993 and we will attempt to make a full reconstruction through April 23, 1993. And let me point out that the combat activities after 19th and through the 24th, the combat activities were subsiding diminishing, and the negotiations were increasing. We will also show the documents showing the Geneva Convention provisions and we will also produce some evidence concerning January 1993. If I am looking at the boxes which I have here, we have emptied about a third of a third box out of five and a half boxes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, he is your witness, Mr. Nobilo. I am just trying to organise things and to see where we are. Therefore, you can consider -- how long do you expect to be working with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This witness will, of course, stay here as long as the Trial Chamber needs him. I believe that it is very important that the Trial Chamber finds out everything they need from this witness. I think that we need another day, day and a half, so I believe that by Thursday morning we could finish with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thursday morning. Thank you. Turning to the Prosecutor, about how long do you expect to cross-examine, Mr. Kehoe? I suppose you have a lot of questions you're going to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I have a couple of questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, we thought so. How long will it take?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In all honesty, I can't believe that if we finish on Thursday morning, that I'll be finished cross-examination by the end of the week. I mean we have, as you can see, I am not giving a rough estimate, 100 exhibits so far --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Two-hundred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Two-hundred exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It will be 200.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It will be 200, whatever. But by the time we finish, Judge Riad, that's 200 exhibits, plus, obviously, the Brigadier's testimony. I am not trying to be vague here, but it will be extensive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The witness will stay until next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. I suppose that my colleagues will also have some questions. Registrar, could we have a private session for just a few seconds. (In private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (In open session).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As we said, we are still at April 17. Can I please have the next document distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness, as regards Kruscica, what was the proportion of the population? What were the different proportions of the different groups in that population?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please turn the microphone on. Brigadier please put the microphone on, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: My apologies. Mr. President, Your Honours, as far as I know, Kruscica was inhabited by Croats, Bosniak Muslims, Serbs and a certain number of Romalija. The most numerous segment were the Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you repeat that? The last sentence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The most numerous part of the population in Kruscica were the Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Riad. Thank you, Brigadier. Mr. Nobilo, will you please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The following is 288, D288A is the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, the Document 288 is basically a report of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade from Busovaca on the 17th of April, 1993. I will read it, it is very short, even though the copy is a poor one. It is addressed by to the command of the Central Bosnia operative zone, "Muslim Armed Forces, MOS launched an attack at 525 hours from Dvor and Grabalj or Gavrine Kuce, Putis and Jelinak. Fighting --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript doesn't seem to be working. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We had some problems with the transcript, but it has caught up with us now and everything is fine. So let me repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: "The Muslim armed forces launched on attack on 0525 hours from Dvor and Gavrine on Gavrine Kuce Putis and Jelinak. Fighting is still in progress. At the moment we are successfully defending ourselves. Similarly they are regrouping their forces in the region of Kuber and Saracevici. The other lines are stable. Information has been received that six buses and two vans have arrived from Kakanj. Everything else okay. Brigade commander, Dusko Grubesic." Brigadier, is this photocopy a faithful replica of the report you received in the morning of the 17th April, 1993, from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the report, the Operative Zone commander had received it. It was sent by the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade and it was registered in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this a faithful copy?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you now please show the Court this new attack? Where was it launched from? The attack that started at 525 hours in the territory of Busovaca municipality. Will you show us on the relief the direction of that attack against Busovaca municipality? Let me repeat, the attack came from Dvor and Gavrine Kuce Putis and Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Gavrine Kuce, this village is on the slopes of Mount Kuber. On this side of the mountain, Gavrine Kuce is here. And Jelinak and Putis are on the left-hand side in relation to the road going from Kaonik to Zenica. If you're going in the direction of Zenica on the left-hand side on the slopes of Mount Kuber are the village of Putis and Jelinak. And on the right-hand side are Gravina Kuce and Gravi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the aim of that attack in your assessment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The aim of the attack was to intersect the road at the intersection of roads, Zenica Busovaca and Vitez Busovaca in the area of the inhabited locality of Kaonik as I have already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Brigadier, the last sentence says: "Information has been received that six buses and two vans have arrived from Kakanj." What does that mean, six buses and two vans? Was somebody in those buses and vans and who?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The buses that came from Kakanj, according to this report, brought with them members of the BH army who were to have been engaged in the offensive operations that were to be carried out in the area of Busovaca municipality. May I add that we often mention Zenica. Mr. President, and, Your Honours, for a better understanding of the balance of forces in the Lasva Valley I wish to tell you the following: Zenica, as a town, had more inhabitants than the whole of Busovaca, Vitez and Novi Travnik together. So that the forces that were in Zenica were more numerous than if we were to add up all the forces that we had. In Novi Travnik I am talking about BH army units even in comparison to the HVO forces in Vitez, Busovaca and Novi Travnik. So, in addition to the forces that were in Zenica and the local forces in the territory of Vitez and Busovaca, I mean BH army forces, reinforcements were coming from Kakanj and Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When the report says six buses, how many men is that for a soldier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That would be about 300 men. And in view of the organisational level of the BH army, that could be described as the strength of a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 289, 289A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we all have before us a report of the Zrinski Brigade from Busovaca dated the 17th of April, 1993, but now at 830 hours. The officer on duty, or rather the Brigade commander, Dusko Grubesic says: "Units from Zenica have lost their positions on Kuber. And they separated from the units of the Zrinski Brigade elevation point 897 and grid points Seracivici are under the control of the BH army. You will be informed of any further activities. Brigade commander, Dusko Grubesic." Tell us whether you recall this document and whether it is a faithful copy of the original document that you had in your hand on that day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I remember the copy, the copy does correspond to the original. It was received by Packet link and it was entered in the register of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command. As we are talking about events of the 17th, I had prepared a map indicating all the major conflicts and artillery operations in the Lasva Valley that had occurred in the course of the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we ask the usher just to take away the cap from the projector so that we can have the map shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Until we come to that map, tell us, you told the Court that Kuber was of strategic importance. What does it mean that the HVO, that units from Zenica, had lost on Kuber the elevation point 897 and grid point Saracevici, and that they were taken over on the 17th of April at 0830 hours by the BH army? What did this mean for the military position of the HVO in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: From the order of the commander of the Operative Zone addressed to the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade saying that Kuber must not fall. In spite of such an explicit order, HVO units did lose a part of Kuber, a part of Kuber. They lost elevation point 897 and a part of the mountain called Saracevica, which means that the road was endangered at Kaonik, and this also shows that HVO units in the Lasva Valley in the territory of Busovaca and Vitez municipalities were endangered by BH army attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map that is being projected has been marked D290.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If possible, can we have it focused?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We'll come to the map later. For the moment, we'll look through all the reports, and only then will we look at the map, towards the end of the day. Let's first examine all the reports.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D291, D291A for the French version, D291B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, for the first time, we see a report by the HVO from Zenica. Something is obviously happening there, so I'll read some key parts. The command of the HVO Zenica and the forward command post of Zmajevac, the date is the 17th of April, 1993, 1020 hours. It is addressed to the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and the heading is "Request." "1) HVO members in the village of Stranjani are under a complete siege, may have been given an ultimatum to surrender their weapons. I have ordered a breakthrough towards the villages of Janjac and Osojnica. Morale is increasingly declining; therefore, I am not certain that the order will be executed. 2) Muslim forces are increasingly surrounding Zmajevac, Cajdras, and Stranjani. They have broken up our sparse forces into groups, and they are trying to disarm and destroy them. 3) Displaced persons are coming to Cajdras. However, Cajdras is being encircled. 4) I will try to reach the village of Cajdras. 5) Please issue urgent instructions for further action and provide us with any assistance as the morale of the fighters is very low." Signed, "Commander Vinko Barisic." First, Brigadier, tell us whether this photocopy is a faithful replica of the original document that reached you from the HVO Zenica at 1020?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It is a faithful copy, and this can be seen from the incoming stamp of the communications centre. All the hand-written notes were written by General Blaskic, and those of us who were working on these documents had certain instructions to go by.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, Brigadier, it says "Commander Vinko Barisic." Wasn't Zivko Totic the commander of this brigade? Let us remind the Court.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This document, as can be seen, was issued on the 17th of April, 1993. Prior to that date, as we saw yesterday, the commander of the Zenica Brigade, today Brigadier Zivko Totic, was abducted and his escort was killed. So that in the case of the Zenica HVO, the first task had been accomplished. The leaders had been removed, so the position of commander is taken over by Vinko Barisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In item 1, Vinko Barisic says that he is not sure that the order will be carried out, his order to make a breakthrough towards Janjac, because of the fall in morale. Why do you think this unit suddenly lost its combat morale, and we will see later on that it was eventually put out of action?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The decline in combat morale occurred because the soldiers of the HVO in the village of Stranjani, let me show you where it is, this is next to Stranjani, right next to Zenica. It is a settlement with a majority Croatian population, and they found themselves totally surrounded, under siege.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In addition to this encirclement, was their morale also affected by the fact that their commander had been abducted?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Certainly. This affected the whole chain of command when it comes to HVO forces in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 292, 292A for the French version, 292B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this document was received by you from the Busovaca Brigade at 12.00. It is brief. It is self-explanatory. There were no important events, so I won't read this document. I should just like you to tell the Court whether this is a faithful photocopy of the original document that you received from the Busovaca Brigade at 12.00?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It is a faithful copy. The document was sent from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade. It reached us by Packet. It was entered in the register of the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 293, 293A for the French version, 293B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, I will read this document, though the copy is rather dark and is hardly legible, but we'll do our best. The Croatian Defence Council, from Vitez, on the 17th of April, 1993, at 1430 hours, to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command, is sending a combat report which reads: "In the zone of responsibility of the Viteska Brigade, during the day today, extremist Muslim forces continued to provoke in all areas of the municipality. Last night, Muslim forces constantly conducted regrouping of their forces in order to realise their sinister aims, that of destroying the Croatian population in these parts and the Croatian Defence Council, the only legal and legitimate armed force which has, so far, already contributed greatly to protect these lands from Chetnik conquest and destruction of Croatian, as well as Muslim, property and lives. In the early morning hours, after evacuating their own population, Muslim forces opened infantry fire on our forces and around 0500 hours started shelling the town. Our forces did not respond to all the Muslim forces' provocations during the night, and they respected the order issued by the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command. After the provocations became more frequent and considerable material damage was incurred to our population's property, our forces responded fiercely and forced the Muslim forces to abandon their sinister plans. During the day today, our forces merely responded to Muslim provocations, aiming exclusively at military targets in order to protect their civilian population from the suffering which they are being subjected to by their extremist leaders. The total number of those killed among the Croatian population in conflict so far is 7 HVO members and 11 HVO members wounded, while the number of civilian casualties is not known. The Muslim forces are continuing to burn our houses in the inhabited areas of Poculica and Gornja Dubravica, from where our population has been expelled." This is hardly legible, because there's a stamp covering the text, and then it goes on to say: "A considerable number of our citizens were arrested, so that in Poculica alone, about 45 citizens have been arrested, among whom there are mothers with small children from the age of two days. We received information in the early afternoon hours that Muslim forces are moving from the direction of Opara village in Novi Travnik in the direction in the village of Zaselje which is gripped by fear and panic among our population. The same are moving out in the direction of Veceriska. We informed Zeljko Sabljic, commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, immediately about this." It is signed by Mario Cerkez, commander of the brigade, though it cannot be seen exactly who drafted this report. Tell me first, Brigadier, whether this photocopy, in spite of it being a poor one, corresponds to the original report received from the Viteska Brigade on the 17th of April at 1430 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The copy does correspond to the original. The document was drafted in the Viteska Brigade. It reached the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. It was entered in the register.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have a specific style of writing here, for instance, reference to the Muslim forces' sinister aims. Is this an example of the type of reporting you referred to in the morning?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. A part of the text in this report is an eloquent example of the kind of reports I was referring to, because commanders or members of brigade commands, due to lack of military training, would write this kind of combat report using terms which are not important for military terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell the Court, as far as you know, what was the educational background of Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez, as of March 1992, was the commander of the Viteska Brigade. As for his education, as far as I know, he had completed a school for qualified workers. This is a three-year school following obligatory secondary education.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to the paragraph on the second page, which I will repeat: "This text was drafted on the 17th of April at 1430. During the day today, our forces only responded to Muslim provocations, aiming exclusively at military targets in order to protect their civilian population from the suffering which they are being led into by the extremist leaders." What do you think? What is the message of this report? Why is this included in his report of the 17th of April at 1430 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: If we remember the order of General Blaskic written in the night between the 16th and 17th and the sentence when he emphasised in block capitals that the civilian population must not be killed, because that is a crime, this commander who wrote this report had received that order, and he is informing his commander that he had conveyed this order to his own subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I think there is no need to dwell further on this document, because it is self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D294, D294A for the French version, D294B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So we have before us document D294. I will read parts of it because this is a report sent by the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade from Busovaca on the 17th of April, but this time at 1800 hours, addressed to you in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. "1) During the day in the zone of the Zrinsjki Brigade Busovaca, Muslim extremists combat activities continued. At 530 hours, a fierce infantry attack was launched by Muslim extremists and oppositions in the region of Kuber and Obla Glava. Muslim fanatics attacked our positions all day with sizeable artillery support from the territory of Zenica municipality. As mortar shells started landing on the centre of the town of Busovaca, a general alert was sounded at 1000 hours as a precaution in order to avoid unwanted consequences. Our positions in the villages of Bare and Dornja Rovna was also under fire all day from the direction of Pezici and Gornja Rovna. There was some occasional fire from the village of Merdani on oppositions in the region of the villages of Strane, Gavrine Kuce, and Podjele" . I will not read the rest of this report, but I should like to ask you whether you recall this report and whether this copy is faithful to the original?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I remember the report. This is a faithful copy of the original. It was sent from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade. It was signed by Ljubo Lovric, whom I know. It bears the stamp of the Brigade and the incoming stamp of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How was it sent? By fax?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This document was received by fax. As can be seen from the indication on the stamp, it says TLF, which means telefax.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, Oblaglava, you've already told us about Kuber, where is Oblaglava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The places of the conflicts referred to in this report are all in the territory of Mount Kuber and I will show them to you on this map. So you see Oblaglava, Kuber is a large mountain where we have both Obla Glava at the foot of which is the village of Jelinak, the village of Putis, then Saracevici. So this is the area where BH army units launched a strong attack. But this report as it was written at 1800 hours, so we must remember the previous reports and the forces coming from Kakanj and Zenica. And we now have on the ground the results of those activities by forces of the BH army brought from Zenica and from Kakanj, which is off the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, let us now read the last report of the Viteska Brigade issued on 2400 hours on the 17th of April and after that we shall try to summarise your recollections with the help of the map to indicate where the clashes were. This is the last document dated the 17th of April at 2400 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 295, D295A is the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is 17th April, report of 17th April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me the English booth did not receive its copy and there is none projected on the ELMO. Can we please have one or the other?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel, nothing that counsel is reading is being translated because they are unable to read it. So if you can just wait until they either get a copy or -- I take it that's the problem in the booth? So if counsel could...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It was on the ELMO, Mr. President, just the video monitor is showing the map and not the document on the ELMO. That's why they're not seeing it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you it is fine now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will read from the top: "This is the Viteska Brigade command of 17th April, 1993, at 2400 hours. It is sending its report to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command." And here we come from the body of text. "During the afternoon hours and especially in the evening hours, after regrouping its forces, the enemy launch infantry attacks from several directions as follows: 1) From the direction of Zenica towards Kuber it was observed that Mujahedeen and other extremist Muslim forces were on the move. Their task was to take control in the Kuber region and then with the support of artillery pieces, make a break through on the stretch Gola Kosa --" I can't read the next word. "Join with Muslim forces in the village of Ahmici and cut off the Kaonik Travnik communication line and join Muslim forces in the Rovna region. Our forces have been trying to withstand fierce attacks from Muslim forces and unable to offer the appropriate resistance. They carried out a temporary retreat to reserve positions. However, upon the arrival of fresh forces, they have successfully retaken the lost positions and the control of a new region. The retreat of our forces provoked a temporary drop in morale among a number of soldiers. However, this lost self-confidence soon returned and in the end it resulted in their return to the previous positions. 2) In the region of Santici village, combat activities were conducted almost throughout the day. The intensity of combat activities was especially pronounced after Muslim forces joined in from the Sljivcica, Sivrino Selo and Pirici direction with constant artillery support from the direction of Poculica and Vrhovine villages. The goal of Muslim attack was to take control of the Santici region and provide support to Zenica and cut off the Kaonik Travnik portion of the road and join in with the Muslim forces in the region of Rovna, Vranjska and Kruscica. 3. Forces of the BH army located in the region of Kruscica village --" I can't read the next couple of words, but it says, "Open intense fire towards the region of Vitez and fired several mortar missiles from the region of Sivrino Bukve to the village of Donja Veceriska, killing two of our soldiers. And in the Kruscica village one soldier was killed and several were seriously and slightly wounded. The material damage incurred to civilian buildings was significant, especially the property of Muslims who sought protection --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the usher please move to the next page. A bit further down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: "The Muslims who had sought shelter and served as a special purposes production. According to the information received from our reconnaissance group there was mortar fire from elevation point 536 on the Rovna and Donja Rovna region in the area of Busovaca municipality. 4) From the Preocica village where the majority of Muslim forces, mostly those who have come from outside of the region have been concentrating and there was an attempt to launch infantry attacks in two directions as follows: The main attack direction was in the village of Tolovici, which they had taken earlier and in the direction of the villages Krcevine and Dubravica with the goal of cutting off the defence line, destroying our positions as well as the civilian population and material goods and breaking through to the Vitez Travnik communication line, taking control of it and further advancing towards Stari Vitez. Auxiliary l forces have been sent in the direction of Poculica village and they joined with the forces in Sljivcica and Vrhovine. This break through of Muslim forces was thwarted and thanks to the high morale of our soldiers, who are mostly from this area, and who are determined to defend these Croatian lands, the enemy's attack was repelled. 5) The part of extremist Muslim forces that have come from outside of the region and local members of Muslim forces from the village of Preocica, Moratovici (phoen), Bukve and Pukovici, as well as part of forces from the village of Klaka (phoen) joined in a fierce infantry attack on the Brdo village where one of our smaller units is located. Considering that the enemy was far superior, both in the strength of troops and materiel and equipment, our units were forced to retreat in the direction of the village of Zabilje. There were no casualties among our troops; whereas the enemy casualties were not reported. 6) Late in the evening, the enemy continued with further acts of provocation along our positions, especially prominent among the enemy activities was sniping on all parts of our municipality. So that we warned our population to be on full alert while in their homes." The signature is illegible so I can't read it. Somebody signed it on behalf of the commander but I can't read the signature. But let me ask you: Can you assist us in this, did you see this document when it arrived from the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Again let me repeat this question, do you recall this document and did you see it on 17th April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I did see this document, it arrived in the Operative Zone command. I remember the contents of the document even though the signature is illegible, I can recognise it. It is Borislav Jozic's signature and he signed it on behalf of the commander Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now again ask you to come to the scale model in order to try to reconstruct the fighting on the 17th of April in the Vitez municipality because this is a document that was drafted at the very end of that day. The judges can see where this fighting took place. First, this is from the direction of Zenica towards Kuber and the Mujahedeen forces were observed, which we are trying to take control of Kuber.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have already pointed this direction towards Kuber and the forces which were dispatched before this time of reporting were not sufficient, so additional forces were brought in to complete the task. See, it is from this direction of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Second, the report says that the fighting went on throughout the day in Santici and then Sljivcica, Sivrino Selo and Pirici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The village of Santici is along the road between Vitez and Kaonik. That is Busovaca Vitez road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, is this the first neighbouring village to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is the neighbouring village. The village of Santici is directly on that main direction of attack of the BH army with the objective of linking up with their forces in Vranjska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Further, the report states that the Muslim forces from the area of Sljivcica, Sivrino Selo and Pirici joined in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This is Sljivicica and Sivrino Selo and Pirici are neighbouring villages to Santici and Ahmici. All this is within an area of one square kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we say that Sivrino Selo, Pirici and Sljivcica were all on a higher ground than the villages of Santici and Ahmici, which are both closer to the road?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, you can see from this model that the Sivrino Selo is leaning on Sivrino Selo which is actually a hill. And also the village of Pirici is sort of a continuation of Sljivcica. I cannot recall the name of this hill here, but you can see clearly the relations between those.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Further on, the report says that the forces which were at these two villages are trying to link up to these other two villages, Kruscica, Rovna, and Vranska. Where are Pirici, Sivrino Selo and Sljivcica in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The Sljivcica hill, Sivrino Selo, and Pirici are to the left, moving from Vitez to Kaonik. The villages of Vrhovine, Rovna -- no, no, I mean, Rovna, Vranska -- my apologies. The villages of Kruscica, Rovna, and Vranska are to the right of the road going from Vitez to Kaonik, and this is where the positions of the HVO were. The HVO positions were squeezed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is to the right of the villages where, you're saying, Vitez is? Are you sure about that? I'm looking at this map here. You're talking about Sivrino Selo and Pirici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in order to follow what I'm pointing at on the scale model, I'm also going to try to point it out on the map which we have on the easel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I want to understand you. On the map, when you go from Vitez to Kaonik, we have the impression that Ahmici and Nadioci are to the left. Santici, I don't see very clearly, at least that's what it seems to me, looking at this map and looking at this one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is correct. That is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you show the villages on the large map on the easel, Sivrino Selo, Sljivcica, Ahmici, Santici. Going from Vitez towards Busovaca, on which side of the road are those villages?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Sivrino Selo, Ahmici, and Santici are in this circle (indicating). It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Which side of the road is that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That is the left side of the road going from Vitez towards Kaonik, that is, towards Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: To the left then, correct, to the left?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President. That is one group of villages where the Muslim forces were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, the other group, please, could you show Rovna, Kruscica, where they are going from Vitez to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: These villages are on the right-hand side, and this is the village of Vranska here (indicating), Kruscica, Vranska, Rovna. These villages are in this circle. I'm going to try to mark them with this pointer. They are situated within a square area of about three square kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On which side of the road going towards Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The village of Vranska, Kruscica, and Rovna are on the right-hand side of the highway going from Vitez towards Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Looking at the map and looking due north and south, Ahmici, Santici, Pirici, where are they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Ahmici, Santici, and Pirici, looking in relation to the Vitez-Kaonik road, are on the north side. Kruscica, Rovna, and Vranska are on the south side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Turn to channel 6 for your interpretation. For the Court, we have forces attacking from the north towards the road. Then we have some forces attacking from the south towards the road. In this combat situation, what, do you infer, is their objective?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The main objective of forces which were attacking in this way is to cut off the communication line, to destroy the command of the Operative Zone, and taking control of the explosives factory in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, is this development something that corresponded to the intelligence reports which we received and about which the previous witness had talked about?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This report corresponds fully with the information which was furnished to us by our intelligence unit in the area of Busovaca and Vitez municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we have the maps distributed, please? This is Exhibit D290. In other words, the map had already been marked for identification. We have it up on the easel, but we also have provided hard copies, and it shows the combat situation on 17 April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like you to analyse the combat situation on the 17th of April, to your best recollection, once we have all of these copies distributed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map is Exhibit D290.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, first, who made this map?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does it represent?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: It represents the development of combat operations in the municipalities of Busovaca, Vitez, and Zenica on 17 April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you agree that the circle would represent the area of combat, the arrows where the artillery shells or projectiles would fall, and the elliptical shape would be where the HVO forces and Croatian civilians were surrounded?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the symbols used in this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you please describe this map in your own words. If you can just summarise your recollections of the day, you don't need to go into every detail. What were the main developments and what were the main problems on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On the basis of the reports which were presented, we have been able to see what the size of the conflict was, the size of the forces deployed by the BH army, and the key areas where the most intense fighting took place. The key problem, the key difficulty, for the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command was the following: The fate of the Stranjani and its inhabitants; also, the fate of the HVO troops and civilians in Podbrijezje, a village, and then the hill of Zmajevac and the village of Cajdras.
