All this, we can see from the reports of the new commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade, Mr. Vinko Barisic. Also, we did not know the fate of the Zenica Brigade commander. Because of this situation, we had the influx of refugees from the Zenica municipality to the Busovaca municipality. As far as the Vitez municipality is concerned, it can be seen that the local forces in the area of Vitez municipality had linked up with the main forces which had arrived from Zenica, and they linked up with the Mujahedeen unit and with the units of the 7th Muslim Brigade. The most significant fighting has been marked here, and I'm going to go in order. It is the villages of Brdo, which, on that day, the army of the BH took control of.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you show the village of Brdo on the map?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It is here (indicating), and it was an exclusively Croatian village. Its inhabitants were exclusively Croatian. The army of BH attacked it. The local troops which were there had to retreat to the neighbouring village of Zabilje, another Croatian village. The next flash point, also very important, was the attack of the BH army units against the troops in the village of Krcevine which is also a village with a full Croatian population. The further attack which took place in the Vitez municipality was Donja Dubravica. This is Donja Dubravica (indicating). Again, this is the attack of the BH army from the direction of Poculica village and Gornja or upper Dubravica. Let me remind you that there's an upper Dubravica and a lower Dubravica. Donja Dubravica was controlled by the HVO, and Gornja Dubravica, upper Dubravica, was controlled by the BH army. The next flash point was a conflict in the village of Santici, Sivrino Selo, and the village -- just a moment, Santici, Sivrino Selo, and Pirici. These villages are directly along the road and near the village of Ahmici. From those villages to the village of Vranska, to the village of Kruscica and Rovna, the distance, that is, the area separating the two forces, Santici and Sivrino Selo, that is, the forces which are at Vranska and Kruscica, is no more than 1.5 kilometres. The next flash point is Obla Glava, Jelinak, Putis. Those are all on Mount Kuber. I recall that the units of BH army took control of both the villages of Jelinak and Putis. The next flash point is the village of Strane and the village of Podjele, the area between Ravno and the village of Bare, and we have constant intense shelling which is shown by these arrows. In other words, Donja Veceriska was shelled; the town of Vitez was shelled; the town of Busovaca and the village of Donja Polje. There was more artillery shelling, but I only marked the very intense powerful shelling on this map. Also, another characteristic of that day was steady sniper fire from the area controlled by the BH army and sniping of the town of Vitez where the HVO units were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In closing right now, are these circles only the main flash points, not any points where the fighting took place on that day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That is correct. These are only the major flash points, but the fighting took place along the entire line of defence where the HVO and the BH army units were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is 1.00. I think it's time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. The hearing is adjourned. We will resume at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.02 p.m. 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please have Colonel Tihomir Blaskic brought in please. Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we had stopped with this map that you compiled and you said that the arrows indicate the places where artillery shells fell. Were they only mortar and artillery shells or were there any other shells as well?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In addition to the artillery and mortar shells, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in its attack on Vitez and Busovaca also used two tanks which were situated in the village of Poculica here. Here. Here, this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, were the tanks there and operating?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, the tanks were in the village of Poculica and they were firing on the Town of Vitez. And not selectively, that is without selecting the targets, but shelling the Town of Vitez as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, Brigadier, on the 17th of April, they used two tanks, how many tanks did the HVO have in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In Central Bosnia, the HVO had no tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that on the 17th of April in the vicinity of Santici, Pirici, there were clashes according to reports. Tell me, near the village of Ahmici where was the front-line on the 17th of April and could you show us on this map where the front-line was established?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, 1993, a front was established about 50 metres or so from the village of Ahmici or more precisely near Alangji (phoen). That position of the HVO on the 17th of April is about 500 metres from the Vitez Kaonik Busovaca Road. I shall try and point it out with this pointer. Here, where the pointer is, that would be the front-line established by the HVO on the 17th of April. That is 50 metres from the last house in Ahmici in Barin Gaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And how many metres from the HVO front-line, and you said that that front-line was 50 metres from the last house in Ahmici, and how far was the front-line of the BH army from the last house in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The distance between the HVO positions and the BH army positions was about 150 to 200 metres, which depended on the location on the ground, so that the front-line was in Barin Gaj outside the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That's north of Ahmici, about 200 metres north of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, did this front-line move at all until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The front-line established on the 17th of April, 1993, between units of the HVO and the BH army remained unchanged until the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is it your opinion that that line was held by local forces from Ahmici or did they receive reinforcements? Did fresh forces come to the assistance of the local forces in Ahmici outside Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In explaining the combat situation on the 17th and the 16th of April, I had mentioned that forces from Zenica had come to the assistance of the local forces in the villages and, therefore, the local forces in the village of Ahmici itself. Those forces arrived and together with those forces, units of the BH army established at the front-line in Barin Gaj in relation to the HVO units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now distribute the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Brigadier Marin, when you say local forces in Ahmici, what do you mean by the local forces in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The local forces in Ahmici were units of the BH army, a unit which roughly the strength of a company because when talking about the organisation of both the HVO and the BH army was that the basic premise was that units should be formed in villages: One village; one unit. If the village was inhabited exclusively by Bosniak Muslims then there would be a unit of the BH army. If a village was inhabited by Croats then there was an HV unit there. If there were mixed villages, such as Ahmici was up to an extent, the Croats joined HVO units and the Bosniak Muslims joined BH army units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The transcript says "HV units", the Brigadier said HVO units, so could the record be corrected, please. Let me ask you once again, were there any HV units there or HVO units, the Croatian Defence Council units?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In Central Bosnia, during the war, there were never any units of the Croatian army. In Croatian villages, in Central Bosnia, there were units of the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document. Can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D296, 296A for the French version, 296B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So we have before us, Document 296. Now we will be seeing a series of orders by Colonel Blaskic of the 17th of April. Up until now we were reviewing the reports he received and now we're looking at the orders. Let me read, "Central Bosnia Operative Zone command, the 17th of April, 1993, at 1850 hours. An order is issued to the Viteska Brigade, the Zrinski Brigade and the 4th Military Battalion. Three units are affected by this order." Preamble: "Because of the intensified attacks by Muslim forces in the area of Kuber and because the safety of the Kaonik Vitez Road may be called in question with the objective of preventing the enemy from seizing and taking control of the said road, I hereby order: 1) With the forces of the Viteska Brigade, the Zrinski Brigade and the 4th Military Police Battalion form a defence line in the wider area of Kuber and link up with forces from Vidovic, grid point 514 to grid point --" I would say it was 646, "Jelinak and Oblaglava, with the following task: To organise a decisive defence on the above-described line and to prevent the enemy advance toward Kaonik and Nadioci at all costs." Item 3 in the second sentence says: "Report to me immediately about all significant changes on the said defence line. 4) Report to me about the execution of this order by 2400 hours." First it said 11 or 77 of April, 1993. Obviously there was some typing errors in the original. "Signed, Commander Colonel Blaskic." Tell me, Brigadier, first, whether this photocopy is true to the original order written by Colonel Blaskic on the 17th of April at 1815 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It is a faithful copy. I personally drafted the document. It was signed by General Blaskic. It bears the stamp of the command of the Operative Zone. The letters ONO refers to me because I followed the implementation of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we say that in items three and four emphasis is laid on the need to report back?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, especially in Item 4 because both the time, the day and the hour is indicated. That is a deadline for reporting because the situation underground was very complicated and difficult and the commanders sought in every possible way to obtain information as to what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you use the pointer to show us the front-line according to this order? Could you show it to us on the relief, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please do so. Will you show us Vidovici and the grid reference point 514 and grid reference point 646 Jelinak, Oblaglava?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This is Vidovici, just above Mahala, which is not mentioned here but it is important to prevent infiltration into Nadioci and the slopes of Kuber and here is the village of Jelinak and Oblaglava. It is rather difficult to show because the line is a winding one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, tell us, is it true that the line was established on the southern slopes of Kuber between the main road or the Lasva River and Kuber?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, the line was established on the southern slopes, actually at the very foot of Kuber right next to the road. More simply speaking from the road to the locality called Gavrine or Jelinak. It may have been a kilometre and a half or two kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does that mean that on the 17th of April at 1815 you had actually lost Mount Kuber and the most dominant features on that mountain?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that can be seen from this order. That we had totally lost the feature Kuber and that it was under the sovereign control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This entire mountain plateau was in their hand, so that the road that we insisted on defending was in jeopardy. And here it says a decisive defence, which means there can be no withdrawal, it has to be defended at all costs. And now the Vitez Kaonik Busovaca Road was endangered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please. Can we distribute it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 297, 297A for the French version and 297B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So the commander, Colonel Blaskic, on the 17th of April, 1993, at 2000 hours is addressing the commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic and Viteska Brigades with an order for reinforcements to Vitez forces. And he says: No. 1, for the needs of the Vitez defences, immediately dispatch a unit numbering 25 to 30 men with the task of preventing the advance of Muslim forces from the direction of the village of Krcevine towards Vitez. First, Brigadier, is this photocopy faithful to the original? Does it correspond to his order of that day and hour?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This order was also written by me. And there is the stamp of the Operative Zone and the signature of the commander of the Operative Zone, General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you show us with your pointer on the map the village of Krcevine and which is the access which is endangered from the village of Krcevine to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Here is the village with a majority Croat population. BH army forces are attacking towards the Krcevine village. If they managed to break through, they would reach the road, link up with the forces in Stari Vitez, endanger the Town of Vitez and link up further with their forces in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The commander is requesting assistance numbering 25 to 30 men, don't you think that this is a very small number in view of the ongoing combat operations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This figure best testifies to the quality of the organisation of the HVO. If the HVO had been structured as a well-organised army, the commander of the Operative Zone would never order a subordinate commander to send him 25 or 30 men or he would send me a company or a battalion or two battalions. So this is an eloquent indication of the state of the HVO in terms of organisation. And it corroborates what I said on the first day and that is that in HVO brigades we didn't have ready, rapid deployment units.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 298, 298A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Here we have another order by Colonel Blaskic dated the 17th of April, 1993, at 2000 hours. The order is addressed to all Brigades, all independent units, the Vitezovi and the communications company. The subject heading is, "Maximum Combat Readiness of the Units." And I am reading: "In keeping with the order of the HVO main staff commander and then hand-written number 02-2/1-01 --" and the rest is illegible. "And due to the open aggression of Muslim forces against the HVO and the Croatian people," then again we see the date written in by hand, "the 17th of April, 1993. I hereby order: 1) All HV units in the zone of responsibility of this command shall raise combat readiness to the highest level. 2) To terminate all R&Rs and prohibit all leaves; to include all able-bodied manpower in the zone of responsibility capable of military service should participate in the zone structure. 3) To break and repel the attacks and the aggression of Muslim forces with all available forces and equipment; to engage all available potentials in the zone of responsibility for the defence and, if necessary, use force. 4) To dig in on the established frontlines and prepare a counterattack. 5) To submit written reports to me every four hours by Packet communications as of the 18th of April, 1993 at 0600 hours. 6) This order shall take effect immediately and unit commanders shall be personally responsible to me for its execution. Commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, can you confirm that this photocopy is faithful to the original and signed by Colonel Blaskic on the 17th of April at 2000 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm it because I drafted the document. General Blaskic signed it, and there is the stamp of the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you explain to the Court, how it is possible that on the 17th of April, the second day of the war, at 2000 or at 8.00 p.m., Colonel Blaskic is ordering maximum combat readiness of units in the sense of banning all leaves and raising combat readiness to a maximum? How can this be explained?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: When the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina launched its attack on HVO units on the 16th of April, certain negotiations were conducted, and we, in the HVO or, rather, in the Operative Zone command, expected the agreed cease-fire to be observed. However, as time went by, the attacks by the BH army gained in intensity. The BH army engaged very large forces. The intensity of the fighting increased. So that on the 17th of April, the commander analysed the situation and opted in favour of such an order. This order also shows, very convincingly, that the commander of the Operative Zone had not prepared attacks on BH army units on the 16th of April, because if we had prepared for an attack against BH army units, we would have, before the 16th, in fact, before the 15th, carried out a general mobilisation. All the things indicated under item 2, we would have terminated vacations and prohibited taking leaves and engaged all our available effectiveness for the attack. However, the gravity of the situation required that the commander should say in item 3 that all available resources should be used to repulse the attack, because we were in a situation of waging a decisive battle, because a step forward in attaining the goal of the BH army, that is, to intersect the road, to destroy the command, to reach the ammunitions factory, and place the whole Lasva region under their control, would lead to the disbanding and disarming of HVO units ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us recall how many command staff members managed to reach the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I said that on the 16th of April, there were seven members of the command staff, and that by the 17th, which we are now discussing, no new arrivals had come, because the road through Grbavica was still blocked, and passage from Busovaca was very dangerous because of constant fire. Members of the command staff who were not in the headquarters on that day did not arrive. The command continued to function with only seven members of its staff present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we proceed to the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D299, D299A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, let me take you back a little bit in time. We had reached the evening of the 17th of April, but now we're going back to the morning of the same day at 0910 hours. Colonel Blaskic is issuing a preparatory combat order for the tying up of a part of the Muslim forces which were attacking the HVO. It is addressed to the commander of the Ban Jelacic Brigade in Kiseljak. This is an order from the 17th of April. "1) The enemy is continuing the intense attack against the forces of the HVO and is trying to completely ethnically cleanse the region of Croats and destroy all the HVO institutions in the Lasva River Valley. The probable objective of the aggressor is, after an accord with the Chetniks regarding the surrender of Srebrenica and other regions, to militarily defeat the HVO and included our regions to some kind of greater Serbia or a new Yugoslavia. In the combats which raged yesterday, the enemy used a much-used method of the Chetniks, keeping women and children in front and using them as human shields, and then occupying the main strategic objects. Nevertheless, they did not succeed, and the enemy forces are concentrating on Jablanica, Konjic, Vitez, and Busovaca. 2) The mission of your troops: Is to tie up the forces of the aggressor in the following way: A) Engage in the blockade of Visnjica and other villages that could be used by the enemy to launch an attack. B) Take control of Gomionica and Svinjarevo after a strong artillery support by the VBR and mortars. The attack of the main forces shall be made from Sikulje and Hadrovci." Then in handwriting, it is added, "Establish a line of defence and keep the troops together." "C) In sector number 5, reinforce the troops at the feature of Badnje (one company) and at the feature of Pobrde (one company). 3) All the attacks of the aggressor have been repelled. The city of Vitez is under our control, and the forces of the Viteska and Busovacka Brigades have taken complete control of the Kuber and Saracevica features, and they have repelled the aggressor's attacks from Zenica. 4) Keep in mind that the lives of Croats in the Lasva River Valley depend upon your mission. This region could become a tomb for all of us if you do not show enough resolve. 5) The time to start this mission will be sent to you from the command upon the receipt of reports stating your preparedness which should be submitted before 2330 hours on the 17th of April, 1993" Brigadier, is this a faithful copy of the order which Colonel Blaskic issued on 17 April at 0910 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise this as Colonel Blaskic's. I recognise his signature and the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On page 1, something was added in handwriting. Can you recognise that handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That is the handwriting of General Blaskic. It is a similar case as we had in some other documents. If he had any comments to make, he would immediately, directly add those comments in handwriting, and the document would then be dispatched in that form.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you tell me, there are many typographical errors. There are lots of errors. Why did you not retype them?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: It would have taken us too much time. We had a member of the command of the Zrinjski Brigade who was not a professional typist and, additionally, we had combat operations going on at the time, so we were in a hurry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us why the Visnjica village was to be blocked and Svinjarevo and Gomionica were to be taken?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On the basis of the intelligence reports which we had, the BH army units were in the largest concentration in the entire municipality of Kiseljak in the village of Gomionica. By taking control of these villages, we would prevent cutting off those enclaves, and we would defend the HVO units in the Kiseljak area. You may recall that the BH army was bringing in reinforcements from Visoko and Kakanj. These preparations were done in order to tie up those forces, the reinforcements, so that we would, sort of, bring relief to the HVO units in the Lasva River Valley so that they could better defend Vitez and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm going to read you another item from this order, and it doesn't sound very military to me. It's on page 2 of this report after a very dramatic statement of the situation which you give. It says under number 4: "Keep in mind that the lives of Croats in the Lasva River Valley region depend upon your mission. This region could become a tomb for all of us if you do not show enough resolve." Why did General Blaskic need to order the Ban Jelacic Brigade into action in such a dramatic way, such an emotional way? Why didn't he just order, "Go ahead. Do such and such a thing"? Wouldn't that have been militarily more proper?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It would have been more proper in military terms. However, as I mentioned, there were very, very few militarily educated officers with proper military training and enough experience. In order to phrase a task in such a way, by using such words, the commander intended to bring home to the officers the seriousness of the situation. This was to find a way for an officer to understand the situation in the Lasva River Valley and the municipalities of Vitez and Busovaca and to act accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does this order sound a little bit like imploring?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: It reflects the situation in which the HVO troops found themselves in Vitez and Busovaca, and it is, sort of, imploring. It is the call of a person who is in desperate straits.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let me show you another document now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D300, D300A for the French version, and D300B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is an order for combat operations of the 17th of April, and the time of this order is 2345 hours. The Defence has received this document from the Prosecution, as can be seen from the number. Can you tell me, do you recognise the stamp and the signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I drafted this document. I signed it on behalf of Colonel Blaskic. This was being drafted all day while he was next door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me, is this order linked to Exhibit 299, the document which we just read?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. That can be seen from the orders that were issued to the individual units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is the goal the same as it was for the preparatory order, in other words, to tie up and alleviate the pressure on the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. That was the key interest of ours at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the basis of this report, does it anywhere state that, in order to carry out this task, civilians should be killed or private property destroyed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D301, D301A for the French version, and D301B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We're reading document 301. This is an order of Colonel Blaskic drafted on 17 April, 1993 at 2210 hours. It is addressed to the commander of the Viteska Brigade and the subject heading is "Organisation and Conduct of Vitez Defence. Order: 1) The Enemy: Wielding overt aggression against the Croatian people and territories, the enemy, the Muslim forces, are trying to completely destroy the HVO and all its installations in the areas of the Lasva Valley, applying the most brutal methods of combat directed against anything Croatian. So far, the enemy has not been very successful but has made extensive use of its advantage in numbers. 2) The task of our forces is as follows: To deploy forces on defence lines and organise a decisive defence; to prevent the enemy from entering the town of Vitez and taking control of the Kaonik-Vitez-Bila road; to organise the defence according to sectors as follows: Sector 1: Zabilje-Brdo-Jardol-Krcevine, grid point 356; Commander of the Viteska Brigade shall name the commander of the sector. Sector 2: Vidovici, grid point 514, grid point 646, Jelinak-Obla Glava; Commander of the Viteska Brigade will also appoint the commander of the sector. Additional sector of Kruscica: To secure the rear guard, Besce, grid point 511, and Baskarad. 3) To carry out 1st level engineer work in the sectors (to dig standing trenches). Deadline is 0500 hours on 18 April, 1993. 4) To organise coordination between the sectors; to make contact in Sector 1 in the left flank of the defence with the Frankopan Brigade units; to apply all measures of combat security while carrying out these activities; to replenish units with weapons to carry out the defence activities; to supply soldiers with two combat sets. In the event of a deficit of formation weapons, appropriate the arms from the other population who is not eligible for military service and use them for this purpose. 5) Commanders of the sector are subordinated to the Viteska Brigade commander. Send reports every four hours with the exact date on the positions of our forces and enemy forces, as well as emergency reports as needed. 6) Commander of the Viteska Brigade is personally responsible to me for the execution of this order. Send me reports about the execution of these orders by 1000 hours on 18 April, 1993. Commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, could you tell me, is this photocopy a fair reflection of the original of the organisation and conduct of the Vitez defence order of 17 April, 1993 at 2210 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I compiled this order on the orders of the commander of the Operative Zone and under his authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now we will move on to 18 April and see where the defence lines were established on that date. First, let's clarify something. In item 3, he's mentioning "1st level engineer work." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That means that the trenches had to be deep enough so that a soldier could stand in it, in other words, that his body would not be exposed anymore, as well as shelter facilities, which means that they have to be covered with earth and wood and any other construction material which was available in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On page 2, he says: "Replenish the units with weapons for defence activities and supply soldiers with two combat sets." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The combat set depends on the type of weapons that the soldiers have. If it is an automatic rifle, a combat set would be 300 bullets, 300 rounds. If it's a semi-automatic rifle, it would be less; if it were an M-48 rifle, then even fewer rounds of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does it mean for the population which is not eligible for military service, appropriate weapons -- first of all, what are formation weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Formation is what a soldier should be issued, given his position in his unit. If we did not have enough, we would probably use something like a hunting weapon, because those were available in the area. Also, you can see that the personnel, which were listed as belonging to the Viteska Brigade, did not all have weapons. We had between 55 and 60 per cent of the weapons that covered the units in Vitez, Busovaca, and Kiseljak. So what we would do, we would then supplement it with hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In 5, it says: "Communications between the sectors are to be organised in accordance with the available communications equipment." Is that also military? Do units usually have a type of communications equipment that is issued to it by formation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. At every level of unit, you have particular communications equipment. Different types of equipment are used for battalions, different equipment for companies, and so on. We used whatever we had in the area. If, in one sector, you had a certain type of equipment, the other sector may not have had it, so they had to coordinate, in the best way they could, how they would establish the link, how they would keep the communication lines open. I would just like to clarify a term that is being used. It's the term "sector," and this order is a bit more detailed than usual. We saw, at the level of brigades in the Viteska Brigade, that was around the 20th of March, 1993, the command of this Viteska Brigade was not yet enabled to fully operate in the event of combat operations in this area. Given the continued attacks by the BH army, I was given an order by the commander to spell out additional details in this order and even draw how certain things should look in the field and which lines should be occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The Viteska Brigade had to have had battalions; battalions had to have had companies; they all would have had to have soldiers. Now you're talking about sectors. You're saying that the brigade commander had to assign the sector commanders. Isn't that a step backwards?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. That was the case, but at that time, the Viteska Brigade had only one battalion which was fully organised. The area of the Viteska Brigade was too large for just a single battalion. So what we did is we started out with having the units in the villages. In other words, there were units deployed in the village. We linked up a number of villages, and from those villages and the area which was covered by these villages, they were then linked together and called a particular sector. It may be best if I can illustrate this by showing you on the map, and let me try to do it from here. If we had a village here (indicating), and we had Krcevine, Dubravica, and Santici, and we said that the area covered by these three villages, this would be to one hill here and another hill over there, that would be one sector. The forces that are supposed to occupy this sector would be the units from the local villages, from Santici and the others. This is how we organised the defence throughout the Vitez municipality, because in the Vitez municipality, we had been completely surrounded. As I said, we had the BH army units which were deployed here in Kruscica, Vranska, and Rovna. It's this area here (indicating), and the BH army units which were here Barin Gaj, Sljivcica, Krtina-Mahala, and Kuber. Where are the HVO units now? They are pretty much right next to the road, to the right and left of the road. From both the north and south side were the BH army units. In a situation like this, the only possibility was to organise the brigade in this way and to defend the town of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, are you telling us that the companies and battalions were not actually acting but only the villages and units in those villages?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is just what I said. We are telling the Brigade commanders to appoint sector commanders because it means that only on the 17th of April was someone to be appointed as commander of the sector to organise defences there. We did not have a commander of battalions or company commanders, which would have been logical and normal in any organised army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you please come to the -- approach the relief and bring with you this document that you wrote yourself and show to the Court where were the defence lines for Vitez municipalities on the evening of the 17th April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I will start from the sector -- from Sector 1, the village of Zablje, which is here from the village of Zablje, there is a road for the sake of orientation this Village Zablje is next to the Bila, Han-Bila Road. So we're going from the left to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please put the little flags there to show where Zablje is. The village of Zablje, the green flag in front of the village of Zablje, not in the village, but in front of it where the Muslim forces were positioned. That's one point. A second, Jardol. Take another green flag and place it in front of the village of Jardol where the Muslim forces were. Krcevine, another green flag in front of the village of Krcevine, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Then TT356. This is a feature, a hill, that cannot be seen here, but it is within the area of Krcevine village. So that is one sector. That is one sector. It is the area here. Then there is a second sector, Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Place a flag there, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Here it is Vidovici. TT514646. This is the position near Mahala. Just a moment, please. Then Jelinak, Obla Glava, which is here. Then we have an additional sector Besce, grid reference point 511, Baskarad. Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, the flags are now indicating the front-line between the Croats and the Muslims on the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 302, 302A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we won't be reading this document. Will you just tell us what it's about?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This is a medical finding for Zoran Pilicic, who was a member of the command of the Operative Zone and he was wounded on the 17th of April, 1993, together with Marco Prskalo, returning from negotiations at the UNPROFOR base and leaving the warrior in front of the main entrance of the building where the headquarters of the Operative Zone was housed. He was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please. We are going on to the 18th of April and we will see the kind of reports that arrived on the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: A small clarification, Mr. Nobilo, you are not presenting all the reports on a particular day. You understand my question? Because the reference numbers of the reports do not follow one another in consecutive order. I assume that you're showing us some of the reports because you just said we are now going to see the reports for the 18th of April. You mean some of the reports for the 18th of April, I assume? Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am thinking of all the reports that the Defence managed to obtain. Naturally, there must have been many more documents circulating in the headquarters. They may have been reports, information, orders, but these are the reports that the Defence has found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So I was just commenting because of the reference numbers. Because very often those reference numbers do not follow one another in an uninterrupted fashion. So I assume that in between there must have been other reports. That was the purpose of my question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is 303, 303A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Talking about these numbers, Brigadier, can you explain to the court how the records were kept; how these numbers were placed on the documents leaving the command and those being received by the commands, internal documents and so on?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: A record of arriving documents, if they came through communication, that is by telefax or by Packet links, those documents would be entered in the communications centre in a register. Those documents would reach the commander. The commander would study it, give assignments to one of the officers in the command and then the document would be entered in the register of the command. The document drafted in the command itself would also bear a number and these reference numbers would follow one another. However, in the case of the 16th, 17th and even the 18th of April, I was telling you of the problems we had in the processing, the person who was the typist also kept the files, so that on some days we didn't have time to register them because we had far more complicated work to do than simply registering documents. So that there may be some lack of order and logic regarding the time a document was received when it was issued and the reference number that figures on the document. I wish to underline that this procedure of filing was not standardised, it was not regulated by the defence ministry, but members in the headquarters and I personally participated on the basis of my own personal experience from the pre-war period, we tried to establish a certain system of bookkeeping ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the incoming stamp would be filled in several days subsequent to the event to the day it was actually received or sent?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know what the number figuring on the documents issued by Colonel Blaskic consisted of? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The first number 01 meant that it was a document of the commander. The second number would be the date and the year -- no, no, the date then the number under which it was registered and then the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am not quite sure that I remember this. Maybe we'll analyse one of the subsequent documents from that standpoint to see if you can remember. So we have now another document, has it been given a number, Mr. Registrar? What is the number of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is 303.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So this is a document dated the 18th April at 0100 hours, report of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade to the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. And the subject is: Disappearance of officers of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. Tell us, in the area of Novi Travnik, was there any fighting on that day, or were they still primarily concerned with the disappearance of their officers?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On the day on which this report was written, there was no fighting between the HVO and the BH army. The key problem for the Brigade was the kidnapping of three officers and their driver, who were taken away in an unknown direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Would the interpreter please say question and answer. Sometimes we don't know who was speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In Novi Travnik, let us repeat, was there any fighting between units of the BH army and the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 304, 304A for the French version, 304B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will read a part of this operative report issued by the command of the Viteska Brigade on the 18th of April, 1993, at 1845 addressed to the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. And it says: "At 1730 minutes, a terrible explosion occurred whose exact location can still not be determined, but it happened between the municipal enterprise Vitkom and the store, Borac. According to data at our disposal and the strength of the detonation, most probably there was an explosives warehouse in one of the houses in the immediate proximity of the store. Because fierce battles were being waged at that time, it can be assumed that the warehouse was hit by a mortar shell, which activated the explosives. On the basis of the intensity of the explosion, one can conclude that it was a matter of a large quantity of explosives. We have no information about any casualties, but one can already affirm that huge damage was incurred. I cannot see the name of the operations officer on duty." Tell us, Brigadier, did you receive this operative report on the 18th of April at 1845 hours from the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, and I remember the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this a faithful copy of the original report you received?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know anything about this explosion that is referred to in this report?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As far as I am aware, this explosion occurred a little earlier than this report was written, a day or two before then. And the place where it occurred was inaccessible for HVO units because it was a place in no man's land between HVO and BH army forces, so that we were not able to establish on the spot the scope of the damage as a result of the explosion. And also my duties in the command on the 16th, 17th and 18th did not give me time to think about this or to analyse this particular event in any detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, have you finished with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In that case we shall have a break and adjourn until ten past four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We can now start with a new document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D305, D305A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we have seen the preparatory order issued by the commander to the brigade in Kiseljak on the 17th of April. We saw the executive combat order sent to Kiseljak by the commander, also on the 17th of April. Now we're going to read the regular combat report coming from Kiseljak on the 18th of April as of 1000 hours. It is addressed to the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and it says: "1) Enemy. A) Chetniks. There are no actions within the zone of responsibility of the HVO and Croatian villages, but Koscan has been attacked severely with artillery. A lot of houses are on fire in Bukovica. B) Muslim armed forces, MOS forces which are fulfilling their tasks in the village of Gomionica, are under attack. They are mostly using snipers. A large number of troops have left Gomionica and pulled out towards the village of Stojkovici. 2) Our forces: Tasks are being carried out according to orders. We have reached Mlava," which is a river. "Fierce fighting is ongoing. We are using artillery and anti-air defence as support. Jahovac, Gromljak, as far as Mlava and Palez, have been disarmed. We have wounded men. We are continuing with the execution of our tasks. We have received zip from the Fojnica Battalion. Everything is ready. They are asking for negotiations. At this moment, the UNPROFOR has come to the commander. 3) Suggestions: None. 4) Requests: Send us reports on situations in the zones of responsibility of other brigades." Signed, "Officer on Duty, Mato Lucic." Tell us, Brigadier, is this a faithful copy of the report you received from Kiseljak, and how did it reach you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: We received the report from Kiseljak by Packet link. This is a faithful copy of the original. I remember the contents. I know Mr. Mato Lucic personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We will distribute another document, and then we will say a few words about the events of the day in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D306, D306A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Document D306 is another report coming from Kiseljak with the same date, the 18th of April, 1993, and the time is 1645 hours. It is addressed to the commander, Tihomir Blaskic, by the brigade commander, Mijo Bozic. The subject heading is "Report. The situation is as follows: The conflict has spread to the villages of Rotilj, Visnjica, Doci, Hrcezi, and Brestovsko. We have lost Zavrtaljka. We did not manage to handle Gomionica, but we did take around 1 kilometre on both sides around Gomionica. Heavy fighting is in progress. We have had three killed and four wounded. The number of missing is unknown." Brigadier, did you receive this document on the 18th of April from Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. We received this document from Kiseljak. This is a faithful copy of the original. The document was received by Packet link, and I know the brigade commander in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day, the 18th of April, one report was received at 10.00, another one at 1645 hours. Outside the facts mentioned in these reports, do you have any other recollections about events in Kiseljak municipality or was your knowledge limited to the facts indicated in these two reports?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: All we knew about events in Kiseljak was what was written in these two reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were these reports linked to the orders received from you on the 17th of April, the previous day, therefore?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us proceed to the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D307, D307A for the French version, D307B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, I will read document D307, actually, a report by the Viteska Brigade of the 18th of April at 0600 hours, and the heading is: "Operations Report for the period between 0000 and 0600 hours. During the night, there were almost no combat activities. We were constantly under intermittent fire from infantry weapons. In the second part of the night, it was observed that Muslim forces were regrouping in all parts of the municipality where their forces are concentrated, and new arrivals of Muslim forces from Zenica were registered, and they are being taken into the regions of Preocica, Brda and Zabilje. During the night, the Muslim population from the village of Donja Veceriska was evacuated in the direction of Bila, Han-Bila. They were evacuated through the mediation of UNPROFOR. In the early morning hours, to be more precise, at 0555 hours, Muslim forces attacked the Croatian population in the village of Divjak. The attack was launched from infantry weapons and three civilians were wounded. Our forces did not open fire and did not respond to provocations by Muslim forces, but, instead, they further fortified the positions taken in accordance with orders from the superior command. Operations Duty Officer, signed," and it doesn't say by whom. Brigadier, is this a faithful copy of the operations report that reached the headquarters at about 600 hours on the 18th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the report and its contents. The command of the Viteska Brigade was far removed from the headquarters of the Operative Zone, so these messages reached us by messenger. Here, we do not have the stamp of the communications centre. So when we come across a report of this kind, it meant that it was carried by messenger to our headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D308, D308A for the French version, and D308B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is another operations report of the Viteska Brigade on the 18th of April, but now at 8.30 hours. The duty officer of the Viteska Brigade has sent it, and it says: "This morning, on the 18th of April, 1993, we have, again, received information on incomprehensible actions by Muslim extremists. According to information from our citizens, who managed to flee their frenzied neighbours, informed us that Muhamed Sivro arrested Marica Kristo, Anto Kristo (taxi driver), his wife and his sister. All the prisoners are from Poculica who fled towards Krizancevo Selo after fierce attacks by Muslim forces. The reason for this arrest, as we have learned, was the alleged disappearance of Muhamed Sivro's son. His son is a soldier in the Muslim forces, and we have established that he was not among those taken captive. This was most probably nothing more than a justification for the incomprehensible actions. The prisoners have been "accommodated" in rooms in the cellar of Muhamed's house where the conditions are intolerable. In this part of Kruscica in the region of Crna Kuca, two Croatian families, who did not manage to pull out, along with our unit located in Lovac, stayed behind. These are the families of Sinisa Jozic (wife and two children) and Jozo Kalemba and his wife. There are indications that they are being held in," and, again, this is hard to read, "a house." We can't really read what it says. "We believe that representatives of UNPROFOR, UNHCR, and Red Cross should be immediately informed about this. Duty Officer of the Viteska Brigade." Brigadier, is this a faithful copy of the operations report of the Viteska Brigade of 830 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the report and its contents, and it reached us by courier, like the previous report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These private arrests, were they typical of those times and those areas in the Lasva Valley? We see that Muhamed Sivro believes that the Croats arrested their son, and so he, in return, arrested some Croats, probably for the purpose of exchange. Was this typical for both sides?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Such an event fully reflects the situation that prevailed in the Lasva Valley during the war between the BH army and the HVO in the Vitez and Busovaca municipalities. There were several such incidents, and we can see from this report, there was such behaviour by BH army members, but similar such actions taken by members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These terms "private arrests, private exchanges," were these terms regularly in use in those days?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. There were such occurrences on both the side of the BH army and the HVO. I wish to point out that the village of Poculica had no HV units in it but, rather, BH army units. Those arrested were living in that village. So there wasn't any conflict, but an arrest did occur for the reasons that the duty officer has given in this report from the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D309, D309A for the French version, D309B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this document consists of a single line, and it says: "Urgent to Operative Zone in Central Bosnia. This morning around 5.30, the headquarters had been attacked from three directions. We are surrounded. Commander Vinko Baresic." It was received on packet. It was received on the 18th of April. Can you also tell me whether you recall this message? Can you refresh your memory? Who is Vinko Baresic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I recall this message. It was received through the packet radio communications. This is a copy of the original. It was received on the 18th of April at 0608 hours. Commander Baresic replaced the abducted Zivko Totic, who was commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade in Zenica. He was in the village of Cajdras. Let me show it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What municipality was this in?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This was in the municipality of Zenica. Both the command and the members of the HVO units are completely surrounded. This is in the village of Cajdras which has a majority Croatian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is the command of the HVO brigade in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The very brief wording of the report speaks of the difficult situation in which the commander and his unit had found themselves in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D310, D310A for the French version, D310B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. The Viteska Brigade command at 1300 hours, and the date is not given, but in handwriting was added "18 April, 1993," sends a report to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command in Vitez. Again, the body of text is hardly legible, but here it is: "Provocations and attacks by extremist Muslim forces have continued during the day. Croatian houses have been looted and destroyed and the elderly people, women, and children who are exhausted have been taken in an unknown direction. During the day today, 20 to 25 Croatian citizens, mostly children, women, and elderly, were arrested in the Grbavica village and taken in an unknown direction. The precise number of those arrested cannot been established because these Croatian houses were, for the most part, located in the village of Grbavica, which is populated mostly by Muslims. The Muslim extremists continue to realise their sinister plans, especially prominent have been sniper activities which are destroying anything that moves throughout the territory of the municipality. The Muslim forces are also still in the process of regrouping. New forces from outside the region are being brought in. A unit of Muslim forces was observed moving from the village of Opara in Novi Travnik along the Has area -- this is probably some kind of mistake -- towards Vitez where they intend to join with the Muslim forces with the villages of Vranska and Kruscica. Last night, one of our members, Josip Livancic, was killed in the Kuber area while Jako Opacak is considered missing and is now believed to have been killed. Our forces are still holding the defence positions under firm control and are not allowing the further advance of Muslim forces. Morale among our soldiers is good," and it was signed by the brigade duty officer, Ivan Sucic. Brigadier, do you recall this document? Is this copy a true reflection of the original?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I do know Ivo Sucic, the brigade duty officer, and this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The text is self-explanatory, but I want to draw your attention to the snipers. Were snipers a serious problem on that day and could you tell us something more about the activities of snipers in the Lasva River Valley?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The sniper activities in the Lasva River Valley in the period we are concerned with was the strongest in the Vitez area which was controlled by the HVO units in the villages of Krcevine. We had significant losses through these activities, both in Krcevine, the town of Vitez, and at Grbavica. I can recall some names, names of persons who were killed by such snipers. For instance, Franjo Nakic's mother, Franjo Nakic was chief of staff. And then a person called Dzambas who was from the unit which came in support to the brigade at Krcevine. A member of the command was killed by sniper. Mr. Borislav Josic, whose report we read here, he was killed in the town of Vitez by sniper fire. Those are the details that I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, did the snipers operate from Stari Vitez, from old Vitez, and which units did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: When I talked about these snipers in Vitez, I was referring to the old Vitez which was under the control of the BH army. So they were operating in the direction of the town of Vitez and were targeting civilians who were in the area controlled by the HVO. All this was at a distance of about 100 metres, so this sniper fire was very efficient. Also, in the case of Grbavica, which was populated partly by Croats, and also in the village of Krcevine, where there were lines held by both the BH army and the HVO, so the sniper fire was used especially where the demarcation lines were very close to one another. In all these three locations, the demarcation lines were less than 100 metres away from one another. So you had the BH army soldiers on the one side and the HVO soldiers on the other side, and they were in places less than 100 metres away from one another. So this sniper fire was very efficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you tell me about Vitez? Were civilians or the soldiers more -- were more casualties amongst civilians than amongst soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The civilians were targeted much more, and there were much more casualties of the sniper fire. I also know that in Grbavica, some children were targeted. They were coming back from the Sunday mass, from church, and they were targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How about the Town of Vitez, did you have to pull a string across the street and cover it with blankets so that citizens could pass through?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, we had to put such protective walls. We had to put them up from the region of the primary school along Tromnice, which is the region separating the village of Komasin (phoen), or rather locally known as the village of Marica. And the section of Old Vitez called Mahala because it was the only path we had available if we wanted to go towards Novi Travnik. Because sniper fire was very dangerous for the main road as well, which was under the HVO control and I'll try to show here. Here is Vitez and the main road. The blue line is the Lasva River. And the road was built here. It's along the river. So from Old Vitez, snipers targeted anyone who passed along this road regardless of whether they were civilians or soldiers. Also, throughout the war the sniper fire was used all the time from Sivrino Selo and the Vitez Kaonik Road was targeted there. And a number of people were killed by this sniper fire. I will try to recall who these people were. For instance, the chief of the civilian police was one among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was there a big canvass which was stretched in the street?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. And it was there until the day of the Washington Accord, so it was there for a full year.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, let's move on to the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D311, D311A for the French version, D311B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next report is from the Zenica HVO. This is also from 18 April, 1545 minutes. And it says: "Military secret, urgent, urgent." So underscored urgent. "Through their aggression, political deceit and deceased in the media. The Muslim force have managed to instil anxiety and fear in a great number of our members. A very complex tactical position of our units is a loss contributed to this. Personnel from the 3rd Battalion of the Second Brigade has already agreed to an agreement with the Muslim forces and the frightened population on the territory of the 1st and the 3rd Brigade will most probably accept this. In the Jure Franatic Brigade, the 1st Battalion with about 100 armed troops is controlling the region around the village of Cajdras as follows: The intersection Cajdras, Paljike, Serusa, Strpci, Osredak, Jezero, Tomnice. It is very hard to hold such a long line with only 200 weapons. The 2nd and 3rd Battalions are under siege and will most probably surrender. At the time of this writing this report, I received information that the Muslim radio is inviting the refugees to return to their homes and the HVO was given an ultimatum to surrender their weapons by 1800 hours. This announcement, this decree, has completely shaken the morale of the remaining soldiers. The troops from Zmajevac are abandoning their positions." And there is an illegible word. "And this will put the village of Cajdras in a very difficult position. Some other officers and myself do not want to surrender. If we were to surrender, I am sure that we would be executed. If it should come to it that the army does surrender, please request our transfer to Vitez or Busovaca through the auspices of UNPROFOR. Here in Cajdras, I saw Colonel Stewart who was willing to do this. It would, therefore, be good if two of his armoured personnel carriers could be here tonight. Please send us urgent instructions what to do. Commander Vinko Baresic." Brigadier, is this photocopy a faithful copy of the original which you received on 18 April at 1545 from Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I know Vinko Baresic. This report was received through Packet radio link and it speaks of a very, very difficult situation in Cajdras on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next report, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D312, D312A for the French version and Document D312B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is the report of 18 April, 1993 of 1600 hours sending central Bosnia Operative Zone command in Vitez. There is no name, just the signature and it's the operations report. "During the afternoon hours yesterday the enemy continued with activities from the Muslim bases mentioned earlier and snipers kept up continuous activity throughout the municipality. The current situation on the defence line is as follows: First, in the Kuber region our defenders are firmly holding the fortified positions. There has been no major combat activity, but an ever larger regrouping of the enemy forces has been observed. We, therefore, need greater support from the HVO Busovaca to assist our defenders in halting enemy attacks. 2) In the Gornij Santici Mahala hamlet there is heavy fighting against far superior Muslim forces who have intensified their attacks from the region of Strpci and Bresce. The villages of Santici, and Dubrava Dubravica are under constant fire by Muslim forces from the villages of Sivrino Selo and Sirotici. We therefore need support of the multiple rocket launchers in order to try to neutralise the most exposed fired positions in the village of Sivrino Selo and thus halt the activities of the Muslim forces. The defence lines on the stretch Krizanicevo Selo, Krcevine and Jardol remain unchanged and there are no major combat activities with the exception of occasional acts of provocation by the Muslim forces from small arms weapons. 4) In the region of Divjak and Bila, our population is exposed to constant shelling and sniper fire from the region of Grbavica. So the move by members of the UN to block our areas in a direction and prevent us from retaliating against the enemy is baffling. It is necessary to send a protest, an urgent protest to the UN forces regarding this behaviour and request of them to treat the Muslim forces and this and other areas in the same way. 5) The region of Kruscica continues to be under attack from Muslim forces from the villages of Vranjska and Gornij Rovna. Negotiations are in progress and we are awaiting results. 6) There is no information from the Brda Zabilje villages since communications with this area have broken down completely. We have requested the UN to visit the region and protect the population from a massacre by the extremist Muslim forces. We have received information that two more defenders have lost their lives and several civilians were wounded. Something is illegible and it probably means that the casualties of the enemy are not known." And it is stamped and signed. Now, Brigadier, do you know, is this a faithful copy of the original which we received on 18 April at 1600 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I recall this report. I recalled receiving it. I remember its contents. All the underlined parts shows that we analysed this report and it has the stamp of the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yesterday we read and today we have had a number of reports. Can you tell me, Brigadier, did you have any offensive attacks in those days in April of 1993 or do these reports truthfully reflect the situation in which you found yourself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In these days, from 16th to 18th April, the HVO units did not undertake any offensive operations because we had no forces to use them in such a way. We were defending ourselves and these reports all reflect the situation that the HVO units were in and the circumstances under which the Operative Zone command worked under.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The locations that are mentioned here, are they the sector that we referred to before the break? So we don't have to show them again.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, the operations officer on duty has adjusted his report to the order he received on the establishment of sectors so as to describe in detail the situation in each sector and each village within the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us proceed to the next report, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 313, 313A for the French version, B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now we have a report from the Busovaca Brigade and the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade on the 18th of April, 1993, at 1800 hours to the central Bosnia Operative Zone command in Vitez. Text: "The situation in the zone of responsibility of the Zrinski Brigade has remained unchanged since our last report. The Muslim forces continue with their combat activities on our positions in the region of Kuber and the villages of Barin Donja Rovna. An anti-air machine gun fired from the region of Crna onto our positions in the Strane village. At 1750 hours an entire heavy attack was launched by Muslim forces on our positions. There were no casualties. All defence lines continued to be quite stable and the morale of soldiers and the logistic support are satisfactory. There are no other observations." Signed "operations officer on duty." I can't read very well his name. I think it's Rajic. Tell us, Brigadier, do you recognise this report? Did it reach your headquarters on the 18th of April and is this a faithful copy of the original?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do remember the report and its content. This is a faithful copy of the contents of the report that reached us from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade. It reached us by Packet link.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D314, 314A for the French version, 314B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It's a report on the implementation of Order No. 01-4-323/93. Dated April 18, 1993, from Busovaca. Let me repeat in any case. It is a report from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade dated 18 April, 1993, and it has to do with the implementation of Order No. 01-4-323/93 addressed to the command of the Central Bosnia operative zone in Vitez and it reads: "Further to your Order No. 01-4-323/93 of 17 April, 1993, we would like to report to you the following: We immediately issued to all our units an order reference No. 774/93 on 17th of April, 1993 at 2100 hours. 1) The combat readiness of the Zrinski Brigade has been raised to the highest level of readiness. 2) All recreation privileges for soldiers have been cancelled and all absence forbidden. 3) All available forces are engaged in combat against the onslaughts on our forces by Muslim extremists. 4) Entrenchment has been carried out on all defence lines in order to organise the defence from the enemy as efficiently as possible. Last night was relatively quiet in the zone of responsibility of our Brigade. The enemy was provoking from infantry weapons and all defence lines. Our units did not respond to the provocations. There were no casualties. Brigade Commander, Dusko Grubesic." My first question, Brigadier, is this a faithful photocopy of the original report you received from Busovaca on the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, we received the document by Packet link from the command of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade and it is a report on the implementation of the order issued by the commander of the Operative Zone to brigade commanders and the actions that are taken by the brigade can be seen from the content of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that the order of the commander of the Operative Zone regarding the abolition of rest and recreation and leave of absence and the raising of combat readiness?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, this order also meant carrying out a general mobilisation of all able-bodied men capable of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us look at the heading which has reference to a number. So let us try and explain to the Court how this reference number was formed in the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, we can see from this number the following: That this reference number of documents consists of the following: 01 is an indication that the document comes from the commander of the Operative Zone. Four, the second number, is an indication of the month. 323 is the number from the files. Slash 93 indicates that the document was drafted in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, this number, which is mentioned in the report of the Busovaca Brigade because the Brigade is referring to it, it is the number of the commander of the Operative Zone. Were only orders filed under this number or all documents signed or issued by the commander Tihomir Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This number 01 was placed on all documents signed by the commander of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, at the time Colonel Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My colleague has indicated in yellow the number we are referring to. And that is the code used by Colonel Blaskic. But, tell me, let us look at the number of the Busovaca Brigade. That number does not apply the same system of numbering. It could have had 0304 or something. It just has a reference number, slash 93. This number has now been coloured in orange. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, we can see from this that in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, there was no standardised procedure for marking documents with a reference number. Therefore, in the Operative Zone command we applied this system. As for the command of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade, it used an entirely different system as can be seen from their reference number, which means there was no standard. And this is also an illustration of the level of development of the HVO organisational structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, just for the sake of clarification, don't answer straight away. Are you wishing to tell us when did this system of numbering begin? It is not urgent that you give me the answer today. For example, the organisation in October, 1992, there was simply the date and the signature of Colonel Blaskic. You don't have to answer me now, I should just like a clarification, when did this system begin to be applied 01-4 and so on? But I am not asking you to answer it straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know because I wasn't there, but I can ask the witness or someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I wasn't there either, so I am asking you to assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D315, 315A for the French version and 315B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we have another report from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade from Busovaca, dated 18th of April, 1993, but at 2200 hours. And since we had several reports on the same day, I am not going to read it. The document speaks for itself. Their Honours will read it. Just tell us whether this photocopy is a faithful copy of the original document that reached the Operative Zone command after 2200 hours on the 18th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it reached us by Packet and it was received by the command of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D316, D316A for the French version, D316B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have a document of the main headquarters of the HVO in Mostar, dated the 18th of April, 1993, addressed to the Operative Zones of Central Bosnia, Bosanska Posavina, Northwest Herzegovina, and Southeast Herzegovina. The subject heading is: "Cessation of Hostilities Between the BiH Army and the HVO.
