Order: On the basis of the conclusions reached after talks between Mr. Mate Boban and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, which took place on the 18th of April, 1993 in Zagreb, and in accordance with point 3 of the agreement, I hereby order: 1) All HVO units shall immediately cease hostilities with the BH army units. 2) The exchange of prisoners, both solders and civilians, shall start immediately. 3) The wounded shall be cared for, regardless of which forces they belong to. 4) Reliable information shall be gathered concerning the protagonists of the conflict, the expulsion of the civilian population, the killing of captured soldiers and civilians, the torching of houses and other buildings. 5) Contact shall be established with the BH army command, asking them to implement the same order. 6) All HVO units shall be familiarised with this order. Chief of Staff of the HVO Main Headquarters, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic." Brigadier, did you receive this order on the 18th of April, 1993 in the headquarters of the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. That can be seen from the stamp of the communications centre. It reached us by packet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in view of the fact that you knew Colonel Blaskic, could it be possible for him not to implement a command of the chief of staff of the main headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That could never happen. As far as I remember, on the basis of this order, we issued our own order for all subordinate commanders. General Blaskic carried out orders of the chief of staff of the main headquarters, to the letter, as they were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My client is telling me that "HV" has been entered in this transcript, and the whole text has to do with the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, not the HV. May that be corrected, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, Brigadier, we've been talking about the 18th. We've been dwelling, at some length, on the 18th. Could you tell us, on this map, where the places of conflict were on the 18th of April, to the best of your recollection? We will distribute the maps in the meantime. Just wait a moment for us to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map bears the number D317.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we proceed with a viewing of this map, you mentioned that, on the basis of the order you received from Petkovic, you issued a new order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I should like to ask my colleague, Hayman, to read that order and distribute it, because it was issued originally in the English language, among others, in English and Croatian. We only have a signed and stamped English language version. Could this document be distributed too, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D318.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The document is titled "The Cease-Fire Between the HVO and ABiH Units, Vitez, April 18, 1993," and is addressed to "Commanders of all HVO Units in Operative Zone Middle Bosnia, UNPROFOR, BRITBAT Commander Colonel Robert Stewart, European Monitoring Mission, 3rd Corps ABiH Zenica. On the basis of the orders given by the HVO head of staff, Herceg office number," number is given, "dated April 18th, in order to completely, I command: 1) All the," appears to be, "subordinate HVO units are to stop immediately all combat actions against the units of the ABiH. 2) Exchange the detained soldiers and civilians at" and then an illegible word. "3) Take care of all the wounded, no matter what army they belong to. 4) Gather the relevant data about the actors of the conflict, the causes of banishing people, murdering civilians and soldiers, burning houses and other buildings. 5) Make contacts with ABiH commands and ask for the adequate command to be given and obeyed completely. 6) This command is to be presented to all the subordinate HVO units. Signed, Commander Colonel Tihomir Blaskic."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you please look at the stamp and signature? Do you recognise the signature of Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the signature of General Blaskic. The stamp is of the Operative Zone command. The document was drafted in the Operative Zone, and it was drafted on the basis of the order we received from the main headquarters of the HVO. Its contents shows that all the activities and actions ordered by the chief of staff of the HVO were passed on to our subordinate units for implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you remember, Brigadier, whether this document was also drafted in Croatian, as well as in English?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that there was a Croatian version of the document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If we have enough time in the next four minutes that are left, if you could indicate on this map of the 18th of April, 1993 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could the registrar give me the number of this map? The number is D317. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you indicate to us, on the 18th of April, where were the areas of conflict between the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, on the 18th of April, 1993, the fiercest clashes in the Lasva Valley, that is, the municipalities of Busovaca, Vitez, and Zenica, between HVO units and the BH army were in the following places: In the Zenica municipality, there's a place called Cajdras. We saw, from the report of the Jure Francetic Brigade in Zenica, what was happening there and what the situation was in the village of Cajdras. In the area of Kuber, and we are now talking about the foothills of Kuber, the villages of Jelinak, Putis, no longer on the mountain itself, because the BH army had gained control of the mountain, but on the slopes of that mountain near the road, there was fierce fighting between HVO units and BH army units. Then, also, Gornji Santici, this is a village in the immediate vicinity of the village of Ahmici. When we were referring to the 17th of April, a front-line had been established there between the BH army and the HVO. In the region of Dubravica, between Poculica and Dubravica, again, a front-line had been established between the HVO and the BH army. In Donja Veceriska, you saw the report that UNPROFOR had evacuated the civilian population, that is, the Muslims/Bosniaks from Donja Veceriska. Then in the area of Divjak, which is a locality next to Grbavica where BH units had considerable forces, in the territory of Busovaca municipality, the area of Gornja Rovna, and the village of Bara, those would outline the places of conflict. Let me now show you the places exposed to heavy shelling on the 18th of April, 1993. The town of Busovaca itself, the locality called Bara, Rovna. In Rovna, part of the population were Bosniak Muslims in Gornja Rovna, and in Donja Rovna were Croats. It was exposed to shelling. Then Grbavica or, to be more precise, this area of Divjak where the conflicts were, and the inhabited area of Stara Bila, those would be the most important localities which were under shelling, fierce shelling, on the 18th of April. In addition to these cases of shelling, I have already reported on sniper fire activities which continued to be most pronounced in the area of the town of Vitez from Stari Vitez, where BH army units were stationed, towards Vitez, where the HVO were situated, and the villages along the road from Vitez to Kaonik, and from Grbavica to inhabited areas of Stara Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, make this map?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We can see from the key, from the legend, what it shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, if this is a convenient time, we could adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn the hearing and resume tomorrow, Wednesday, at 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
